toolsFull.name: assert_logcat
toolsFull.description: VERIFICATION PRIMITIVE — wait up to timeoutSec for a logcat line matching `pattern` (optionally scoped to `tag`) to appear, polling a bounded dump. Turns an app's Log.* markers into a machine-checkable pass/fail signal so an agent can PROVE behavior instead of eyeballing it (e.g. assert 'rayCast HIT' after attaching a collider, or 'placed pin #' after a commit). Returns {matched, line, elapsedSec, serial, logWindow} — matched:false is a normal (non-error) result so callers can branch and escalate; status:'inconclusive' means the window's marker was never seen in the bounded dump (nothing was matched against the unscoped buffer — re-run). Nothing here clears the device log. Typical loop: open a window (clearFirst:true, or write your own marker with adb_shell `log -t pico-mcp <marker>` and pass sinceMarker) → trigger the action (launch / drive input) → assert_logcat.

serial.description: adb device serial (default: the sole connected device / emulator)

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against each logcat line, e.g. 'rayCast HIT' or 'placed pin #\\d+'

tag.description: Restrict to this log tag (logcat <tag>:V *:S), e.g. ClaimSightPin

clearFirst.description: Opens a marker window instead of clearing the device log; equivalent to sinceMarker with a fresh marker (kept for compatibility — use when re-running the same assertion so stale lines cannot match). Nothing is erased.

sinceMarker.description: Match only lines logged AFTER this marker line (e.g. one you wrote with adb_shell `log -t pico-mcp <marker>` before the action). Takes precedence over clearFirst. A marker absent from the bounded dump makes the result inconclusive — never a match against the unscoped buffer.

maxLines.description: Bound on each raw dump (`logcat -t <n>`) of a WINDOWED read — one opened by clearFirst:true or named by sinceMarker. Without a window there is nothing to slice after, so the poll dumps the whole buffer and this input is inert. logd applies the bound to the selected buffers BEFORE the tag filter, so on a chatty device a small tail can drop the window marker while the filtered output stays short — the result is then inconclusive, never a false pass. Default 20000 (the module default of 4000 suits short reads; this tool polls for up to 180 s). Raise it for a long poll on a busy device: `-t <n>` never returns more than the buffer holds.

toolsFull.name: inspect_bundle

toolsFull.name: decode_spatial_bundle
toolsFull.description: Decode what the PICO Spatial Editor BAKED into a compiled .bundle — the agent's window into the editor's output without opening the GUI. Parses the embedded AssetInfo.json (spatial::asset::AssetInfoMap) and returns a histogram of asset TYPES (mesh / texture / shader / materialinstance / collisionshape / physicsmaterial / scene / …) plus the per-asset guid→name→path→type list, with collision/physics/scene assets called out. Note: a `collisionshape`/`physicsmaterial` asset being present means the editor cooked the USD CollisionComponent into the bundle — but that does NOT make Scene.rayCast hit at runtime (the runtime needs a CollisionComponent attached to a live entity + a PhysicsWorldComponent; see diagnose symptom=raycast_no_hit / generate_collider_kotlin).

full.description: Include the full per-asset list (guid/name/path/type); default returns the histogram + collision/physics/scene assets only

toolsFull.name: bake_textured_model
toolsFull.description: Bake a TEXTURED 3D model (GLB/GLTF/USD/USDC/USDZ) into a renderable PICO .bundle via spatialbundle, then verify the texture + material actually baked. This is THE way to import a textured mesh/world (e.g. a World Labs Marble GLB) so it RENDERS in-app: spatialbundle bakes a PHYSICALLY_BASED material + ASTC texture, and you load the BAKED model. (Raw-GLB runtime loading renders BLACK because gltfio's async texture loader is never driven; and you must NEVER `prepend references=@x.glb@` inside a USDA — USD has no glTF plugin, you get an empty bundle. Pass the model path here instead.) Load the result with: AssetBundle.load("asset://<bundle>") then Entity.loadSuspend("<modelName>", bundle). Baking leaves generated assets/BundleCache/ content; exclude BundleCache from APK assets with androidResources.ignoreAssetsPattern and add app/src/main/assets/BundleCache/ to .gitignore.

outBundle.description: Output .bundle path (copy into app/src/main/assets to ship it)

compressTextures.description: ASTC texture compression (astc6x6 is a good size/quality default)

toolsFull.name: scene_schemas
toolsFull.description: Return PICO's custom USD schema definitions (SpatialComponent / SpatialAudio / SpatialTimeline) from the installed toolchain — the authoritative grammar for authoring PICO USDA scenes as plain text.

toolsFull.name: measure_model
toolsFull.description: Measure a .glb/.gltf model's REAL world-space bounding box, so surface placement never runs on hand-measured numbers. Walks the scene graph, composes each node's transform, and unions the POSITION accessor min/max that glTF requires — exact, no buffer decoding. Returns size, min/max, centre, meshNodes, and baseLift (the distance from the model's origin down to its lowest point). Feed size straight into generate_surface_placement_kotlin's modelSize and baseLift into its baseLift: get the height wrong and the model sinks through the floor or hovers above it; get the origin convention wrong and it is buried to the waist. Downloaded and generated models (Meshy, Marble) are usually origin-CENTRED rather than sitting on their base, which is exactly the case that looks fine in code and wrong in the headset. Warns when the scale looks like centimetres. This is the measuring step of the model->MR pipeline: measure_model -> bake_textured_model -> generate_surface_placement_kotlin.

modelPath.description: Absolute path to the .glb or .gltf to measure

toolsFull.name: wait_for_log
toolsFull.description: Block until a regex appears in logcat (or timeout). Essential for an agent loop: wait for 'scene loaded', an app-ready marker, or an error, instead of sleeping a fixed time. By default it opens a marker window first, so only lines logged after the call can match; the device log is never cleared. Returns {matched, elapsedSec, serial, logWindow, lines}; a window whose marker is never seen is an inconclusive error, never a match against the unscoped buffer.

pattern.description: Regex to match against new logcat lines

clearFirst.description: Open a marker window before waiting (recommended): only lines logged after the window opens can match. Nothing is cleared; false polls the whole buffer.

maxLines.description: Bound on each raw dump (`logcat -t <n>`) of a WINDOWED read — the one clearFirst:true opens. With clearFirst:false there is no marker to slice after, so the wait dumps the whole buffer and this input is inert. logd applies the bound to the selected buffers BEFORE the tag filter, so on a chatty device a small tail can drop the window marker while the filtered output stays short — the wait is then inconclusive, never a false match. Default 20000 (the module default of 4000 suits short reads; this tool polls for tens of seconds). Raise it for a long wait on a busy device: `-t <n>` never returns more than the buffer holds.

Writes the .usda; pack it with pack_bundle/iterate_scene and verify with inspect_bundle. Use import_asset first to bring meshes/textures into the project.

toolsFull.name: gui_capture
toolsFull.description: Capture the PICO emulator's GUI window — a macOS host-window view. Use it as an alternate LOOK path when adb screencap is black or omits intended immersive pixels; that asymmetry occurred in some Unity runs but did not reproduce for a later same-moment OpenXR run, so it is not a universal renderer rule. The GUI free-cam can drift across launches. For native/shell content, capture_frame is usually the simpler headless path, but neither path proves appearance until its returned pixels are LOOKed at and ledger-bound. Tries window-id capture, then screen-region capture. Requires macOS Screen Recording permission.

windowId.description: Specific window id (default: the main/largest emulator window)

mode.description: window=by id, region=by screen bounds, auto=window then region

toolsFull.name: gui_camera
toolsFull.description: Drive the emulator's WASD camera mode by sending keystrokes to its GUI window (the ONLY way to move the head/camera — gRPC head-pose is gated). Sends a sequence of keys (W/A/S/D move, Q/E up/down, arrows look). Requires macOS Accessibility permission AND that you have FIRST clicked into the emulator window to enter camera mode (mouse-drag enters it; keystrokes alone may not). Verify the result with gui_capture.

keys.description: Keys to press in order, e.g. ['w','w','a','d']. Single chars; 'left'/'right'/'up'/'down' for arrows.

holdMs.description: Approx press duration per key (via repeated keystrokes)

toolsFull.name: gui_permissions

toolsFull.name: compose_inspection_scene
toolsFull.description: Build a complete ClaimSight-style spatial inspection scene: an environment (procedural damaged room, or a referenced GLB/splat room from e.g. World Labs Marble), severity-colored damage markers pinned in 3D using the canonical ClaimSight 5-tier palette (1 green→5 purple) and real damage taxonomy. All geometry uses real bound MATERIALS (ND_UsdPreviewSurface, emissive cores) — NOT primvars:displayColor, which renders white in the PICO runtime. Writes renderable USDA; pack with verify_scene/iterate_scene. Markers carry damageType/severity as USD customData. NOTE: referenced GLBs must be TEXTURED meshes to look right — an untextured collider mesh renders dark.

asset.description: For glb: a TEXTURED mesh filename. For skybox: a 360 equirectangular IMAGE filename (under Sources/Assets; import_environment first).

toolsFull.name: generate_surface_placement_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Seat a BAKED model on a DETECTED real-world surface (FLOOR/TABLE/WALL/BED/CABINET…) — the MR placement recipe, generated instead of hand-written. Emits a self-contained Kotlin object whose seat(root, add) detects the plane, converts anchor space into the scene root's space, seats the model with the right base lift, and attaches a PRIMITIVE box collider plus the required PhysicsWorldComponent. It bakes in five silent traps measured on 2026-07-29/2026-08-06: a one-shot plane query returns 0 while Stage entry is still settling (so it POLLS), floor height comes from the plane, anchor space needs root.convertPositionFrom, downloaded/generated models are origin-CENTRED, and mesh shapes—although queryable from runtime and loaded assets—use local vertex coordinates plus the collider entity transform, so imported node offsets/display scale can misalign them. This generator deliberately uses the declared-footprint box for predictable alignment and lower query cost. Pair with bake_textured_model. REQUIRES an open Stage — any stage style, Mixed (1) included; a WindowContainer returns 0 planes ('Full Space' in older notes meant open-Stage, not stageStyle 3).

toolsFull.name: place_model_on_surface
toolsFull.description: ONE CALL from a .glb/.gltf on disk to Kotlin that seats it on a DETECTED real-world surface — chains the proven v30 steps measure_model -> bake_textured_model -> generate_surface_placement_kotlin so their numbers are wired, never retyped: modelSize/baseLift come straight from the file's accessors, modelName/bundle come from the bake. The underlying recipe is emulator-proven end-to-end (ledger com.picoagent.mrtable seq 10-11: the generated placement built into the real mrtable app and re-seated itself after a COLD restart — planes=40 after 7 retries, FLOOR at y=0.40 — LOOKed at); this orchestrator is that same chain composed, and the bake step RUNS the local spatialbundle toolchain (not a dry run). Emits the 6-trap seating object: polls for planes, takes height from the plane (never a constant), converts anchor space, applies the MEASURED base lift, attaches a PRIMITIVE box collider + PhysicsWorldComponent, and seats a FLOOR model in FRONT of the user. Returns the wired Kotlin + baked bundle + insertion instructions + measured dims/baseLift. REQUIRES an OPEN Stage — any stage style, NOT a WindowContainer (a WindowContainer returns 0 planes; 'Full Space' in older notes meant open-Stage, not stageStyle 3); stage style 1 (Mixed, the default) shows the real room behind the model.

toolsFull.name: generate_ecs_system_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit an ECS Component + System PAIR plus its registration snippet — PICO's own per-frame mechanism, the one the engine drives. Returns JSON {files:{'<Name>Component.kt','<Name>System.kt'}, registration, note}. Prefer this over generate_scene_animator_kotlin for NEW per-frame behaviour: System/SceneUpdateContext/EntityQueryCondition is what PICO's samples use, the engine ticks it (no hand-rolled coroutine loop to leak), and per-entity state lives on the component. SceneAnimator remains valid and vision-verified for runtime-built entities. WHAT IT GETS RIGHT, each grounded in the 0.13.3 sources jars and cited inline in the emitted Kotlin: a top-level class with a public no-arg ctor (registration reflects via getConstructor().newInstance(), System.kt:106); a clone() override that copies every field (clone() is OPEN not abstract at Component.kt:205, and the base impl silently drops subclass state); a HOISTED EntityQueryCondition.hasComponent (customCondition/or force a full scene scan, Scene.kt:270-282); deltaTime-scaled motion (SceneUpdateContext.deltaTime is seconds); in-place TransformComponent mutation on the batched-JNI path rather than a per-frame component replacement; and a paired registerSystem/unregisterSystem DisposableEffect. TRAPS IT ENCODES: never cache context.scene (one global System instance is ticked once per CONTAINER per frame with a different scene, System.kt:53,111); registerSystem is a silent no-op unless SpatialBuild.isSpatialPlatform(), so systems never tick under JVM/Robolectric; and the registering module needs ui:foundation, not just core. Kinds: spin (yaw), orbit (phase on the component so a constellation can be spread), bob (vertical oscillation), custom (correct scaffolding with a TODO body). HONEST STATUS: vision_verified on emulator-5554 (ledger com.picoagent.v35expc#0, 2026-08-06). The SDK logs 'SpatialPack: [main] register SpinSystem' and the motion was MEASURED rather than eyeballed: across captures 1.6s apart only the entity carrying the component changed, while the sphere/capsule/backdrop regions came back RMSE=0 (bit-identical) — which excludes head pose, compositor noise and lighting drift. Also measured: a HOME+resume cycle yields exactly ONE register and no unregister, so the emitted DisposableEffect does not double-register, and the pairing is scoped to COMPOSITION (the container's lifetime) rather than app foreground/background — a registered system keeps ticking while the app is backgrounded.

toolsFull.name: generate_attachment_panel_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit Compose panels placed INSIDE the 3D scene at a chosen position in metres — the in-scene counterpart to generate_panel_compose_kotlin's docked 2D Activity. Returns JSON {files:{'SceneAttachments.kt'}, usage, note}. RETRACTION THIS SUPERSEDES: we shipped 'no public API positions an auto-hosted 2D panel in world space' and compiled placement:'world' to a head-docked fallback. That is true only of an OS-composited 2D Activity window, and it stays true for that case — but inside a SpatialView, AttachmentPanel(id, size, alignment, content) yields a Compose surface backed by a real ECS Entity whose TransformComponent you set, in metres. It has been public in 0.13.3 the whole time (ui/foundation content/SpatialView.kt:182); six of PICO's eight samples use it. SCOPE, STATED PRECISELY: this is scene placement, not world-LOCKING — panels live in the hosting SpatialView's local space and move with their container; a pose fixed to the real room still needs AnchorComponent and remains deferred. TRAPS IT ENCODES, each grounded and adversarially re-verified: the attachments lambda is NOT a composable scope (SpatialView.kt:81), so panelSize() is hoisted into a separate rememberAttachmentPanelSizes(); position is METRES but size is PIXELS; the Dp overload of panelSize is emitted because the metres overload throws outside a spatial container (LocalPhysicalLengthConverter is compositionLocalOf{error}); panelSize is remember-ed with no keys, so sizes are frozen at first composition; the attachment entity must be explicitly added via content.addEntity or it silently never renders; and alignment is the anchor point ON THE PANEL aligned TO the entity in normalized [0,1], not a world offset. Panels are SpatialUI inside PicoTheme, never Material. faceViewer uses LookAtComponent.setViewerAsTarget() — there is no BillboardComponent in 0.13.3. STATUS: VISION_VERIFIED on the emulator (ledger com.picoagent.v35attach#0) — a panel from this tool renders in-scene and correctly occludes geometry behind it. It also draws its own background: an attachment has no container glass behind it, and PicoTheme's default text colour is black, so without a fill the panel is invisible over dark scene content (found by looking).

toolsFull.name: generate_container_app_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit a Main.kt with MORE THAN ONE container — a DefaultWindowContainer or DefaultStage root plus secondary WindowContainers and Stages, opened and closed at runtime through LocalSpatialNavigator. Returns JSON {files:{'Main.kt'}, note}. WHY: generate_app_wiring has always emitted DefaultStage for every app, but PICO's WelcomeSpace (the Week-1 curriculum anchor) declares three containers in one mainApp and navigates between them, so an agentic track limited to DefaultStage cannot reach a comparable outcome by prompting. FOUR RULES IT ENCODES, each read from the 0.13.3 sources jars and adversarially re-verified: (1) a DECLARED container does not open itself — WindowContainer(id=...) only registers it, something must call navigator.openWindowContainer(id), which is very likely why our own measurement said an app's own WindowContainer never appears; (2) the obvious Stage teardown is BROKEN — closeStage is suspend, and DisposableEffect{onDispose{scope.launch{closeStage()}}} silently never runs because a rememberCoroutineScope is cancelled before onDispose, so we close on a LifecycleEventObserver at ON_PAUSE/ON_DESTROY like PICO's own samples; (3) Stage has NO style parameter — immersion is declared via the Immersion(...) factory (its class ctor is internal) and the style is chosen at openStage time; (4) Modifier.windowConstraints belongs to WindowContainerConstraintsScope, so it exists only inside WindowContainer content, and under ContainerResizeType.ContentSize it is what actually sizes the window. It deliberately does NOT emit the manifest meta-data keys for style/worldscaletype/defaultsize — those resolve through framework stubs absent from 0.13.3 and their encodings are KDoc-only; the DSL parameters are the verified path. (5) every container's content needs its OWN import — `contentImport` per container, not just rootContentImport. Without it a multi-container app whose secondary content lives in a subpackage (which is what our own scaffold does) failed to compile while this tool reported success; that gap was found by building the output rather than reading it. HONEST STATUS: vision_verified on emulator-5554 for BOTH container kinds. WindowContainer: ledger com.picoagent.v35expb#0. Stage: ledger com.picoagent.v35expc#2 (2026-08-06) — a declared secondary Stage DOES open on navigator.openStage(id, style, bundle), and the Bundle CROSSES the boundary intact (receiver read StageScope.bundle and got back exactly what was sent). Also measured: opening the second Stage REPLACES the first — the DefaultStage content stops rendering, matching Stage.kt:73 'When Stage is opened, the system will hide windows from other apps'. So a Stage is not a second window you add; it is a takeover.

toolsFull.name: generate_skeletal_animation_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneSkeletal.kt — play BAKED skeletal clips from a loaded model (Entity.load -> findSkinnedMeshEntity -> getAnimationResources -> playAnimation). WHY IT EXISTS: we had no generator for this, so any GLB with baked clips — most character content an agent would download — was un-animatable through our toolchain. Our other two lanes are procedural only: SceneTween/SceneOrbit bake a clip from a TweenAnimation, and SceneAnimator drives TransformComponents per frame; neither can play a clip that already exists inside a model. FIVE TRAPS IT ENCODES, each grounded in the 0.13.3 jars and PICO's own Animation sample: (1) PROVENANCE DECIDES DISPOSAL — clips obtained from a MODEL are MODEL-LIFETIME (never use{}, never closed on stop or when switching clips, closed exactly once at teardown), whereas clips you GENERATE are per-use and yours to close; same type, opposite policy, and PICO say so three times in their own source; (2) findSkinnedMeshEntity searches THIS ENTITY AND ITS CHILDREN, so it runs on the parent you added the model to, not the loaded root; (3) only Entity.load may leave the main thread — findSkinnedMeshEntity/getAnimationResources/playAnimation/stopAllAnimations are @MainThread with a runtime check and throw on Dispatchers.IO; (4) a non-skinned GLB returns an EMPTY array silently with no exception, so the feature becomes an invisible no-op unless you log it; (5) clip lookup is BY NAME via AnimationResource.getName(), because positional indexing is a hard contract with the GLB's clip order — a bounds-checked positional form is emitted alongside for callers who authored the model. transitionSeconds crossfades: AnimationPlayConfig's DEFAULT transition mode is CROSSFADE for skeletal. (6) A CLIP PLAYS ONCE. AnimationPlayConfig has NO loop field — it carries only transitionDuration/transitionMode/blendLayer/blendWeight (AnimationPlayConfig.kt:27-54); looping is AnimationResource.repeat(count) (:62), which CREATES A NEW resource. So an un-repeated walk cycle finishes in under a second and the model stands still, which reads exactly like 'the animation never played'. The repeat()-derived resource is APP-created and therefore ours to close — same type as the model's clips, opposite policy, which is trap (1) applied to a derived resource. HONEST STATUS: PARTIALLY verified on emulator-5554 against PICO's own rigged asset (pico_robot_animated.glb from the 0.13.3 Animation sample), ledger com.picoagent.v35expc#3. VERIFIED: Entity.load builds the hierarchy (both skinned meshes present with ModelComponent in a live scene dump), findSkinnedMeshEntity returns 2 entities, getAnimationResources returns 5 correctly-named clips [idle, jump, look_around, walk_forward, wave], repeat() succeeds, and playAnimation throws on neither entity. NOT VERIFIED: the model never RENDERED and no motion was observable — across every capture the only changing pixels in the frame were an unrelated control object. Placement and scale were confirmed correct in the scene dump (PICO's own constant 0.0045 for this asset; at scale 1 the model is ~222x human size and you stand inside it). Unresolved and stated as a hypothesis only: PICO's Animation sample ships an editor-asset module, so the raw-GLB path may need the bundle pipeline or environment lighting our scaffold does not provide. Do not claim visible skeletal animation from this generator without a capture.

toolsFull.name: generate_event_subscription_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneEvents.kt — the SDK EVENT BUS (content.subscribe(eventType, subscriber): Cancellable), covering collision, animation and audio events in ONE generator because they share one bus. WHY IT EXISTS: before this, grep for CollisionEvents / content.subscribe / AudioEvents / AnimationEvents across our whole codegen returned nothing — generated apps could SIMULATE but not REACT, so 'ball hits pin -> score' had to be polled from the agent bridge instead of handled in-app. FIVE THINGS IT ENCODES, all jar-cited: (1) subscriptions are held in a LIST and all cancelled — an app subscribing to three event types with one Cancellable? silently leaks two, and PICO's own SpatialMesh sample never cancels its collision subscription at all, so we follow the sample that gets it right; (2) it emits the direct concrete-class-literal form rather than the samples' generic `when (event) { X::class.java -> }` wrapper, which only compiles thanks to Kotlin's equality-based smart cast and is a trap for a generator; (3) CollisionEvents.Exit carries ONLY entityA/entityB — no position, impulse or contacts, unlike Enter/Update — so payload handling is generated per event rather than assumed uniform; (4) THE REPORTING PRECONDITION: collision events fire only when at least one body is DYNAMIC, so two static colliders touching fire nothing silently, and the escape hatch is PhysicsWorldComponent.kinematicCollisionReportMode (default NONE) — stated in the emitted file because 'my handler never fires' is otherwise unsearchable; (5) event.contacts is EMPTY under the default BRIEF detail level, which gives averaged position and accumulated impulse only — DETAILED is what populates per-contact data. (6) THE MIRRORED-DELIVERY TRAP, measured not read: the bus delivers every collision TWICE from a SINGLE subscribe — once as (entityA,entityB) and once as (entityB,entityA), same averaged contact point, ~1ms apart — so a raw score++/sound/spawn handler double-counts every hit, and nothing in the signature or KDoc says so. The emitted file collapses the pair with an orderless guard keyed on Entity.id (Entity.kt:126; names are not unique), and Exit clears the key so a bounce still re-fires. HONEST STATUS: verified on emulator-5554 (ledger com.picoagent.v35expc#1). A dynamic sphere dropped on a static pad fired 6 raw events and exactly 3 after the guard (Enter, Exit, Enter — the bounce survives); a static box resting on a static box fired ZERO, independently confirming the dynamic-body precondition in (4). Animation and audio events remain structural — not yet exercised on device.

toolsFull.name: generate_bundle_lease_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneBundles.kt — ONE AssetBundle per path, shared across callers, refcounted by OWNER, closed when the last owner releases. WHY: five of our generators (app wiring, surface placement, environment, data binding, signage) each call AssetBundle.load independently, so an app using three of them loads the same bundle three times. v35.5 fixed the single-owner case inside data binding with a keyed cache; this is the cross-generator, multi-owner case, where the same model can be live in a list, a detail view and the scene at once and must survive any ONE of them letting go. PROVENANCE, stated honestly: the conformance report said to model this on WelcomeSpace's AssetBundle.kt, but that refcounted manager exists only in the 6.0.0 GitHub copy (83 lines) — PICO's authentic 0.13.3 archive has 29 lines and just a lazily-loaded shared singleton. So NO 0.13.3 sample demonstrates this pattern; what makes it safe is that every SDK call it needs is confirmed in the 0.13.3 jars (AssetBundle.load :470, releaseModel :213, close :235, valid :82). THREE THINGS IT ENCODES: owner-keyed refcounts so release(path,'preview') cannot free a model the room still holds; a re-check of AssetBundle.valid before every use, because a cache that hands back a CLOSED bundle fails far from the cache; and a Kotlin Mutex rather than synchronized, because acquire suspends on IO and two concurrent acquires would otherwise each load their own copy. HONEST STATUS: structural — jar-cited, not sample-demonstrated at 0.13.3, and not yet built or looked at.

toolsFull.name: prepare_environment
toolsFull.description: Auto-detect an incoming environment asset (360 image / textured GLB / untextured collider GLB / Gaussian splat) and route it onto the path that actually RENDERS in the PICO USD runtime. Parses GLB glTF headers inline (counts materials/textures/images + checks for TEXCOORD_0 UVs) to tell a textured mesh from a bare collider. A 360 equirectangular image becomes a SKYBOX (the best visual path — surrounds the user, fixes falling out). A textured GLB should be routed through `bake_textured_model` (a baked bundle renders textured — raw RUNTIME-loaded GLB is what renders black, not baked meshes). An untextured collider can be pano-PROJECTED to a textured GLB via headless Blender then baked, when Blender + a panorama are available, else imported as a dark collider. Gaussian splats (.spz/.ply) DO load natively on PICO 0.13 (GaussianSplattingComponent) — use `import_world_environment` (vision-verified, a 1.92M-pt SPZ on the emulator) or generate_environment_kotlin kind='splat'. Copies the chosen asset(s) into Sources/Assets and returns the exact `environment` object to pass to compose_inspection_scene.

sourcePath.description: Absolute path to the asset (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.exr/.hdr 360 image, .glb/.gltf mesh, or .spz/.ply splat)

projectDir.description: The spatial app project dir (asset is copied into <projectDir>/Sources/Assets)

skySphere.description: Optional: a panorama image (abs path or a filename already in Sources/Assets) to project onto an untextured collider GLB via Blender

toolsFull.name: list_environment_assets

GLBs are header-parsed (textures + TEXCOORD_0) to distinguish textured meshes from bare colliders.

projectDir.description: The spatial app project dir whose Sources/Assets is listed

toolsFull.name: diagnose
toolsFull.description: Self-diagnosis knowledge base: given a SYMPTOM you observe in the PICO spatial runtime (white/invisible geometry, black/black-textured environment, tiny panels, dead buttons, scattered/hovering pins, falling out of the room, build failures, nothing rendering, no controller pose, Scene.rayCast returning no hit), returns the verified root cause, concrete fix steps, the DESIGN.md rule it violates, and the tools to apply the fix. Use this to self-correct instead of guessing.

rootCause.description: The verified root cause from the knowledge base.

designRule.description: The DESIGN.md rule or repository source the symptom violates.

relatedTools.description: Tools that apply or verify the fix.

toolsFull.name: design_review
toolsFull.description: Orchestrate a VISUAL self-review of the live emulator scene: captures the emulator GUI free-cam window (same path as gui_capture; this view can drift across launches), runs cheap pixel heuristics (brightness / contrast / color variety) to flag obvious candidates, and returns the IMAGE plus a DESIGN.md rubric for YOU to evaluate. Heuristics and path choice are not a LOOK. capture_frame is the headless alternative, but a black frame from either route is inconclusive until another path is inspected. Pair a confirmed defect with diagnose.

windowId.description: Specific emulator window id (default: the main/largest window).

checklist.description: Include the DESIGN.md review rubric in the response (default true).

toolsFull.name: generate_collider_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit a verified, drop-in Kotlin file (SpatialColliders.kt) that gives a native PICO spatial app WORKING Scene.rayCast surface collision — the keystone for landing pins/markers on walls/floor/ceiling and for object picking. Encodes the hard-won on-device recipe: a PhysicsWorldComponent on the scene root is REQUIRED (USD-authored collision never becomes a query actor); primitive shapes (box/sphere/capsule) are proven queryable in every case measured, which is why this tool emits them. REFUTED 2026-08-06, ledger com.picoagent.v35expc#4: mesh colliders are queryable from a RUNTIME MeshResource AND from a LOADED asset — createStaticMesh and createConvexMesh both answered rayCast against a primitive control in the same cast. The real trap is ALIGNMENT: the cooked shape follows the mesh's LOCAL vertex data and the collider entity's own transform, not the source model's node hierarchy, so it often does not contain the entity origin and can shrink to millimetres under the model's display scale — verify by sweeping, never with one ray at the origin. createBox uses FULL extents; the public 5-arg CollisionComponent ctor; no RigidBody needed. Provide a `room` AABB to get a 6-wall box room, and/or `shapes` for arbitrary primitive colliders. Returns Kotlin + integration notes.

packageName.description: Kotlin package for the generated file, e.g. com.example.claimsight.content

room.description: Emit a 6-wall box room collider at this AABB (you stand inside; rays hit walls from inside with inward normals)

kind.description: Primitives only in THIS generator — cheapest per query and no alignment reasoning. Mesh shapes ARE queryable (ledger com.picoagent.v35expc#4); build those yourself from a MeshResource when you need the real silhouette.

size.description: box: FULL extents (x,y,z). createBox takes full extents, faces at +-size/2

shapes.description: Arbitrary primitive colliders (box/sphere/capsule) at world positions

rayCastHelper.description: Include a rayCast(scene, origin, dir) helper

toolsFull.name: generate_environment_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit verified, drop-in Kotlin to load a RICH 3D environment into a native PICO app. kind='skybox' = an equirect pano on a large inward sky-sphere (unlit) — from a FIXED viewpoint it fills every direction; kind='splat'/'texturedMesh' add real depth. IMPORTANT (verified with camera movement): ALL of these are added via SpatialView, which renders content inside a BOUNDED VOLUMETRIC WINDOW — if the viewer moves ~1m out of that volume the content clips to a 'portal' and the rest goes to void (the C4 stage-vs-window ceiling). None of these is a truly boundless environment like the system home env; that is not achievable via SpatialView in SDK 0.13.3. kind='texturedMesh' must be baked first (raw GLB renders black). Mesh/splat need a box-collider rig for Scene.rayCast.

assetFileName.description: Skybox: the equirect pano PNG/JPG (e.g. world_pano.png, ≤4096px). Splat: the .spz/.ply. Mesh: the .glb.

baseColorImage.description: texturedMesh only: the base-color PNG/JPG filename

delivery.description: storage = adb push to the app's external files dir; assets = ship in the APK (skybox uses assets)

rotationEuler.description: environment euler degrees — Marble splats usually need y=180; default 0,180,0 for splat, 0,0,0 otherwise

scale.description: uniform scale (default 1; mesh worlds often want ~2.2 for a large walkable space)

skyboxRadius.description: skybox sphere radius in m (default 30 — large enough to read as infinity).

eyeHeight.description: skybox: viewer eye height to center the sphere on (default 1.6).

toolsFull.name: run_visual_regression
toolsFull.description: Run a snapshot diff through the GUI free-cam window. This host-window view can drift across launches, so use it only against a deliberately refreshed baseline. regression_gate can diff adb forward frames when that route actually contains the app view; a black/absent view is inconclusive, not a clean regression sample. Steps drive launch/input, capture by macOS window id, and diff with ImageMagick or sips; the method is reported. updateBaseline writes current captures. Missing window/Screen Recording permission returns a structured error.

projectDir.description: Spatial app project dir (informational; reserved for project-scoped defaults)

baselineDir.description: Directory holding baseline PNGs named <step>.png (also where updateBaseline writes)

outDir.description: Where to write current captures + diffs (default: a temp dir under pico-mcp/regression)

name.description: Step/frame name; the baseline is baselineDir/<name>.png

tapText.description: Regex (case-insensitive) of a clickable UI node's text/desc to tap before capturing

keyevent.description: adb keyevent to send before capturing, e.g. KEYCODE_ENTER

launch.description: Package name to (re)launch via the LAUNCHER intent before capturing

settleMs.description: Delay after the action before capturing (default 1200ms)

steps.description: Scripted sequence; omit to use the built-in ClaimSight sequence (home/armed/placed)

threshold.description: Max normalized diff [0..1] a step may have before it counts as a regression

updateBaseline.description: Write current captures into baselineDir as the new baseline instead of diffing

packageName.description: Package to launch for the built-in sequence (default com.pico.claimsight)

gridN.description: sips fallback downscale grid (NxN); ignored when ImageMagick is used

serial.description: adb device serial for the scripted actions (default: sole connected device)

toolsFull.name: generate_scene_understanding_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit drop-in Kotlin (SceneUnderstanding.kt) that uses PICO native scene-understanding (sense/plane) to land markers on detected surfaces (floor/wall/ceiling) — the native equivalent of WebXR hit-test. RETRACTION (2026-07-28/29, measured): the emulator DOES supply scene understanding — a FULL SPACE app receives ~40 SIMULATED planes with semantics (FLOOR/TABLE/CHAIR/DOOR/WINDOW + BED/WALL/CEILING/CABINET), orientations and metre bounding boxes; you MUST POLL, because a one-shot query during Full Space entry returns 0 (warm boot ~4 one-second retries, COLD boot ~7; FLOOR is at y=0.40, not 0 — the historic '0 planes' belief came from one-shot queries). REAL-room surfaces remain hardware (Swan). MESH: RETRACTED 2026-08-06 (ledger com.picoagent.v35expa#1) — mesh data DOES work on the emulator: 44 distinct anchors, via both subscribeAnchorUpdate and loadAllAnchors. The old 0 was a readiness race, and note that state==RUNNING is NOT a readiness signal (both trackers report RUNNING while still returning 0 for ~1-2s), so POLL until non-empty rather than gating on state. Includes dumpPlanes(maxRetries) for the legacy PLANES| lane and registerAgentBridgeSceneSnapshot() for revision-41 lossless file transport: one query_scene_anchors command performs consecutive unfiltered non-empty reads and preserves full transforms, vertices, indices, and duplicate/order-preserving raw semantic assignments without geometry log lines. REQUIRES Full Space (an open Stage); a WindowContainer returns 0 planes.

agentBridgePackage.description: Package containing generated AgentBridge (default: replace trailing .content with .agent, otherwise append .agent).

toolsFull.name: probe_planes
toolsFull.description: Dump the LIVE plane inventory (label / orientation / pose / extent / retry count) from a RUNNING app — institutionalizes the poll-for-planes lesson (2026-07-29: a one-shot query returns 0 during Full Space entry; a cold boot needed ~7 one-second retries; FLOOR at y=0.40). Drives the injected Agent Bridge: broadcasts AGENT_CMD cmd=dump_planes, then parses the PLANES| logcat markers that SceneUnderstanding.dumpPlanes() emits. REQUIRES the app to (1) hold an OPEN Stage (Full Space — a WindowContainer returns 0 planes), (2) have generate_agent_bridge injected, and (3) register the command: AgentBridge.register("dump_planes") { _ -> CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).launch { SceneUnderstanding.dumpPlanes() } } (SceneUnderstanding.kt from generate_scene_understanding_kotlin). Returns an honest error naming the missing prerequisite when no markers appear. STRUCTURAL evidence (logcat markers) — it proves what the runtime reports, not what a human sees.

applicationId.description: App id whose Agent Bridge to drive, e.g. com.example.spatialdemo (action = <id>.AGENT_CMD).

serial.description: adb device serial (default emulator-5554).

tag.description: Logcat tag SceneUnderstanding logs under (default SceneUnderstanding).

waitSec.description: How long to wait for the PLANES| dump (dumpPlanes itself polls up to 15s on an empty room).

toolsFull.name: decode_editor_project
toolsFull.description: X-ray a whole PICO Spatial Editor project (a SpatialPackContent tree OR an Android project root that contains one). Reports: project name/version, every scene (.usda) with its prims/materials/shaders/components/asset-references, the Sources/Assets inventory categorized by type, and the editor's baked hidden dirs — .Library (processed assets), .Component (custom components), and .CacheData (BundleCache manifest: bundleTool version + bundled scene list + md5; MaterialCache material count). This is the agent's view of the editor's GUI state without opening the editor.

projectDir.description: Path to a SpatialPackContent dir, or an Android project root (it will descend into editor-asset/src/main/res3d/SpatialPackContent). ~ is expanded.

toolsFull.name: author_materialx
toolsFull.description: Emit a PICO Spatial Editor MaterialX (.mtlx) material in the editor's exact format (MaterialX 1.38). mode=pbr -> UsdPreviewSurface (the editor default); mode=unlit -> ND__unlit_surfaceshader (guaranteed-bright, lighting-independent). bright:true mirrors the editor's own self-lit trick (emissiveColor=diffuseColor) so a PBR material renders bright instead of dim. Optional baseColorTexture wires an <image> node (MaterialX standard) — NOTE: hand-authored image textures are known to pack BLACK on this runtime except via an editor material or the bake path, so the textured .mtlx is built-for-editor/headset, not emulator-verified. Format copied verbatim from real editor MaterialCache output.

name.description: Material display name (header comment only; node names stay editor-canonical). Default 'Material'.

baseColor.description: Linear RGB triple, e.g. [0.8,0.8,0.8] (default). For unlit this is 'color'; for pbr it's diffuseColor.

bright.description: PBR only: set emissiveColor = baseColor so the surface self-lights (the editor's own bright trick). Ignored for unlit (already bright).

baseColorTexture.description: Optional base-color texture path/filename to wire via an <image> node. UNVERIFIED on this runtime (see note) — prefer bake_textured_model for textured meshes.

includeStdlib.description: Emit the editor's stdlib xi:include block (default true; matches real editor .mtlx). Set false for a minimal material.

toolsFull.name: capability_report
toolsFull.description: Emit a caller-supplied capability matrix gated by VISUAL GROUND TRUTH. This legacy report can accept a linked human-looked vision_verified row, but cannot authenticate producer-specific device_verified, auto_judged, or usd_host_render provenance; those requests are downgraded to structural with the correct producer route. Ledger-generated reports preserve those tiers after their producer gates.

appName.description: App or build name for the report header.

name.description: Feature, e.g. 'baked textured environment' or 'sense/plane surface pins'.

status.description: How it was verified. Producer-specific device_verified/auto_judged/usd_host_render values are accepted only to return an explicit structural downgrade; use their named producer tools.

evidence.description: The proof: for vision_verified, the capture path + what was seen; else a logcat line / 'xmllint well-formed' / etc.

ceiling.description: The emulator ceiling gating this feature (for headset/blocked items).

features.description: Every feature in the build and how it was verified.

summary.description: One-line bucket counts, strongest evidence first.

deviceVerified.description: An agent LOOKED at a same-serial device capture and its live raw adb identity passed the PICO-shaped/non-emulator lineage gate; this is not cryptographic device attestation.

visuallyVerified.description: An agent LOOKED at a linked capture.

autoJudged.description: Calibrated eye scored it — measured, not human-seen.

builtForHeadset.description: Compiles for Swan-only capability; deferred honestly.

markdown.description: The same matrix rendered for humans.

toolsFull.name: generate_agent_bridge
toolsFull.description: Emit an INJECTABLE Kotlin 'Agent Bridge' library that makes a native PICO app headlessly agent-drivable and structurally inspectable. It self-initializes via a manifest-merged ContentProvider and exposes AGENT_CMD broadcasts, structured logcat telemetry, a live scene-graph dump, and the revision-41 query_scene_anchors transport. Scene geometry uses a versioned, lossless, nonce-addressed app-cache JSON file read with explicit-serial run-as; it is never sent through logcat. Those signals prove state, not appearance. Pair them with a capture whose returned app pixels you actually LOOK at; adb capture_frame is often stable for native content, while an alternate host-window capture may be needed when it is black/inconclusive. Returns Kotlin, manifest wiring, and drive examples. APIs are source-confirmed; broadcast/logcat behavior is emulator-measured; revision 41 was live-validated on emulator-5554 with the generated com.fleet.swanmissiontable app. Geometry and labels retain a structural evidence ceiling; rendered pixels require separate visual evidence.

packageName.description: Package for the bridge files, e.g. com.example.spatialdemo.agent

toolsFull.name: capture_frame
toolsFull.description: Capture a frame with `adb exec-out screencap` (headless, no macOS perms) and return it as an image the agent MUST visually inspect. ROUTE: this composites the CURRENT DISPLAY through the device shell — for the checked runs that display carried the forward immersive view, but for an XR-runtime immersive layer the same command can return black while the app renders correctly, so a black frame is inconclusive about the route rather than a rendering verdict. The bytes are structurally inspected (signature, chunk CRCs, raster) before being returned; a truncated or non-image capture is refused instead of saved. This is the ground-truth check: code/logcat prove a thing EXISTS, only looking proves it RENDERS correctly. Downscales for the response and also saves full-res to disk. Content outside the captured field of view (e.g. pins in a ring behind the viewer) won't appear; reposition/navigate to inspect the rest.

serial.description: REQUIRED adb device serial. There is no default: a frame names the device it came from.

outPath.description: Full-res PNG output path. Default: a run-unique RETAINED file under the observation root, never a fixed shared path a later capture can overwrite.

maxDim.description: Max dimension of the returned (downscaled) image (default 1200).

toolsFull.name: capture_settled
toolsFull.description: Capture one exact adb serial until two consecutive rendered PNG byte streams are identical. Returns settled, timeout, or capture_failed with exact runtime binding, hashes, attempts, and the last valid external frame. A timeout is NOT a navigation waypoint even if its pixels are later LOOKed at. Evidence ceiling is structural; LOOK is still required for any pixel claim. Byte-exact hardware/MR settlement remains UNVERIFIED and is refused.

serial.description: Exact online adb serial; required so the tool never guesses among emulator/device targets.

outPath.description: Absolute external full-resolution PNG path (default: a unique /tmp/pico-render path); repository paths are refused.

maxDim.description: Maximum response-image dimension (default 1200; full artifact is unchanged).

comparison.description: Phase-1 comparison policy; only byte_exact is supported.

priorSha256.description: Prior reviewed frame SHA-256. In stable mode, a matching pair is ignored for backward compatibility; transition_then_stable additionally labels the transition and stability phases.

mode.description: Settlement mode (default stable); transition_then_stable requires priorSha256 and must be selected explicitly.

deadlineMs.description: Single monotonic settlement deadline budget in milliseconds.

attemptTimeoutMs.description: Per-screencap timeout, clamped to the remaining deadline.

toolsFull.name: query_scene_anchors
toolsFull.description: Query one receipt-bound running app for a versioned, lossless Agent Bridge mesh snapshot. Readiness is established from consecutive UNFILTERED non-empty reads before labels are applied, and drift covers every transition in that accepted streak. Raw geometry and repeated semantic assignments go only to a private external artifact; returned labels may select anchors, but semantic alignment stays unverified and triangle relations are refused. The topology policy also governs reported SDK label-set changes; numeric transform and extent bounds always remain mandatory. Terminal statuses are ready, label_absent, not_ready, stage_not_open, bridge_unavailable, stage_mismatch, invalid_payload, or binding_failed. Evidence ceiling is structural.

serial.description: Exact online adb serial; never inferred.

labels.description: SDK label names applied only after unfiltered mesh readiness.

toolsFull.name: navigate_to_scene_target
toolsFull.description: Select one fresh largest-horizontal scene target, bind its exact runtime and qemu window, and run bounded guide acquisition/calibration/navigation through settled shared camera routes. Output remains structural and every returned diagnostic requires an explicit LOOK.

pollMs.description: Scene-readiness polling interval in milliseconds (default 1000; maximum 60000).

toolsFull.name: emulator_look
toolsFull.description: AIM the emulator's free camera by a mouse-drag, then capture the rendered frame and return the image — so you can VISUALLY verify a whole scene, not just the forward view. The emulator only enters look/orbit mode on a RIGHT-button drag (keystrokes/left-drag do nothing). dx<0 looks left, dx>0 looks right; dy pans vertically. A ~300px horizontal drag is a sizeable yaw; call repeatedly to sweep around. Requires macOS Accessibility for the controlling process. Pairs with capture_frame (which captures without moving). The frame is saved to a run-unique RETAINED file under the observation root, never a fixed shared path a later look can overwrite; the default TARGET is unchanged (emulator-5554).

dx.description: Horizontal drag pixels from window center (negative = look left, positive = look right). ~300 ≈ a big yaw.

dy.description: Vertical drag pixels (default 0). negative = up, positive = down.

button.description: Mouse button for the drag (default 'right' — the one that orbits).

serial.description: adb device serial (default emulator-5554).

capture.description: Capture + return the frame after moving (default true).

toolsFull.name: capture_orbit
toolsFull.description: DRIVE the emulator free camera (walk keys + look drags), settle, then capture the HMD frame — the primitive that lets an agent verify 3D placement from angles OTHER than the launch-forward view. Moves run in order: {key:'w'|'a'|'s'|'d'|'q'|'e', holdMs?, repeat?} walks (gRPC sendKey; W fwd/S back/A left/D right/Q down/E up relative to facing), {dragDx, dragDy} rotates the view (right-button CGEvent drag). The camera has INERTIA: this tool settle-waits until two consecutive captures are byte-identical before returning. Phase 1 requires the serial-bound macOS qemu-window lane; non-macOS rendered motion remains UNVERIFIED and is refused. LOOK at the returned frame before claiming anything about the scene.

key.description: Walk key: w=forward s=back a=left d=right q=down e=up, relative to current facing

holdMs.description: How long to hold the key (default 600 ms ≈ a large step)

dragDx.description: Right-drag pixels: rotation. dx>0 looks right, dx<0 looks left (macOS only)

dragDy.description: Right-drag pixels: dy>0 looks down, dy<0 looks up (macOS only)

moves.description: Sequence of walk/look moves, applied in order

serial.description: adb serial (default emulator-5554)

outPath.description: Where to write the full-res capture (default /tmp/pico-render/capture_orbit.png)

maxDim.description: Max dimension of the returned image (default 1200)

capture.description: Capture + return the frame after moving (default true)

toolsFull.name: capture_multiview
toolsFull.description: Capture one scene from FOUR viewpoints in a single call — front (current pose), high-angle (fly up + look down), and two side obliques (strafe + re-aim) — then walk the camera back and report whether the round trip closed. This is the multi-angle visual check that placement work MUST pass: a single forward view cannot verify a 3D layout (two sessions were lost to that). Each leg settle-waits out the free-cam inertia and aborts before further motion if settlement or an action is uncertain. Phase 1 uses the serial-bound macOS qemu-window lane. LOOK at every returned frame: check nothing intersects furniture/walls/rug from ANY of the angles.

serial.description: adb serial (default emulator-5554)

sideHolds.description: How many 600ms strafe holds per side leg (default 3)

aimSideDrag.description: Re-aim drag px toward subject after strafing (default 200)

upHolds.description: How many 600ms up-holds for the high angle (default 2)

aimDownDrag.description: Look-down drag px for the high angle (default 260)

toolsFull.name: author_editor_component
toolsFull.description: Emit an editor-format USD component block (Collision BOX / Audio file / Audio mixer / Timeline) to nest under a prim in a Spatial-Editor scene (.usda). Collision uses the exact instance format the editor wrote (verified) — NOTE: text collision needs the editor BAKE to register physics (use generate_collider_kotlin for working runtime rayCast). Audio/Timeline conform to the editor's authoritative schema.usda and are round-trip-checked by packing through spatialbundle. Returns the USD text + where to attach it.

name.description: Prim name for the emitted def (default per component).

mixerGroupPath.description: audio_file: prim path of a SpatialAudioMixerGroup.

targetPath.description: timeline: prim path the action targets.

asJson.description: Return JSON {usd, attachUnder, note} instead of raw USD.

toolsFull.name: decode_editor_settings
toolsFull.description: Parse a Spatial-Editor project's UserSettings ECS files (which decode_editor_project skips): EditorEnvSettings.json (skyboxColor/useColor/environmentIdx/intensityExponent/rotation) and EditorContainerSettings.json (containerType/planeSize/volumeSize/unitType), plus the per-user YAMLs. These are the file LEVERS editor_op edits.

projectDir.description: SpatialPackContent dir or an Android project root (~ expanded).

toolsFull.name: editor_project_diff
toolsFull.description: Snapshot a project's decode, then report the STRUCTURAL delta after an edit or build (scenes/prims/materials/components/asset-refs added/removed, assets by type, and whether the bundle was REBUILT via targetMd5). First call (no baseline) saves a snapshot; later calls diff against it. This is how a headless editor_op verifies its effect.

projectDir.description: SpatialPackContent dir or Android project root.

snapshot.description: Force (re)save the baseline instead of diffing.

toolsFull.name: editor_op
toolsFull.description: Apply a whitelisted editor FILE LEVER headlessly (the honest editor_op — the editor has no scripting/RPC; file-edit + rebuild is the only headless authoring path). op=set_skybox_color (EditorEnvSettings skyboxColor+useColor), set_environment (environmentIdx+intensityExponent), set_stage_size (EditorContainerSettings planeSize/volumeSize). Edits the committed ECS JSON and returns before/after. NOTE: whether the headless build consumes these is UNVERIFIED — pair with editor_project_diff after a rebuild to confirm the effect (and back up the file; this mutates it).

projectDir.description: SpatialPackContent dir or Android project root.

toolsFull.name: assert_scene
toolsFull.description: STRUCTURAL scene verification via the injected Agent Bridge: broadcasts dump_scene, parses the live entity tree from logcat, and checks assertions (entitiesPresent / minEntities / componentsPresent / markers). Requires generate_agent_bridge injected + attachScene called. PROVES existence, NOT appearance — pair with capture_frame / verify_visual for the visual ground truth.

applicationId.description: App id whose Agent Bridge to drive, e.g. com.example.spatialdemo (action = <id>.AGENT_CMD).

serial.description: adb device serial (default emulator-5554).

entitiesPresent.description: Each name (substring match) must appear in the dump.

minEntities.description: Total entity count must be >= this.

componentsPresent.description: Each component class name must appear on some entity.

markers.description: Each substring must appear in the CURRENT dump's AGENTBRIDGE| stream (a marker window is opened before the dump and only lines after it count, so launch-time events like scene_attached won't be here — use dump_end / entity names / your own per-dump markers). The device log is never cleared.

toolsFull.name: verify_visual
toolsFull.description: WHOLE-SCENE visual verification: capture the forward frame, then orbit the emulator camera by a fixed yaw and capture again, N times — returns the frames as images so the agent can LOOK at the entire scene (not just forward). Optional baselineDir does a coarse perceptual diff (ImageMagick) to flag regressions. The agent's eyes are the verdict; the diff is a coarse signal (free camera, not pixel-repeatable).

serial.description: adb device serial (default emulator-5554).

steps.description: Number of frames in the sweep (default 3).

stepDx.description: Per-step yaw drag in px (default 340; sign sets direction, + = look right).

baselineDir.description: Optional dir of baseline frames (frame_0.png ...) to perceptual-diff against.

toolsFull.name: bundle_content_diff
toolsFull.description: Deterministically diff the COOKED CONTENT of two .bundle files via `spatialbundle info` (cooked models/assets/deps by name/type/path — no timestamps). This is the reliable 'did the bake change' signal that bundle md5 can't give (the bundle file is non-deterministic). Returns added/removed content lines + model/asset counts + whether content is identical.

toolsFull.name: verify
toolsFull.description: The verification GATE: combine STRUCTURAL truth (assert_scene — Agent Bridge dump_scene + assertions) and VISUAL ground truth (verify_visual — orbit-sweep capture) in one call. Returns the structural pass/fail AND the rendered frames to LOOK at. Use before claiming a build works: structural = exists, frames = looks right; you must inspect the images, not just the pass flag. Requires generate_agent_bridge injected for the structural half (visual half works regardless).

applicationId.description: App id for the structural half, e.g. com.example.spatialdemo.

serial.description: adb device serial (default emulator-5554).

entitiesPresent.description: Structural: entity names that must be present.

componentsPresent.description: Structural: component class names that must be present.

steps.description: Visual: frames in the orbit sweep (default 3).

baselineDir.description: Visual: optional baseline frame dir for a coarse perceptual diff.

maxReturned.description: Visual: max frames returned as images (default 4).

error.description: Present when status=error (e.g. Agent Bridge unreachable).

baselineDiffs.description: Coarse perceptual diffs vs baselineDir, when one was given.

toolsFull.name: editor_export_bundle
toolsFull.description: Editor-parity bake: pack a scene dir to a .bundle via spatialbundle (the editor's packer) and report the COOKED assets, confirming cooked physics (collisionshape + PhysicsMaterial) that raw USD lacks at runtime. Use after author_editor_component (Collision) / author_materialx to produce a deploy-ready bundle. Returns cooked-asset counts + physicsCooked flag. Cooked physics is decode-verified here; rayCast HIT is a runtime/logcat check (assert_scene), appearance a capture check.

sceneDir.description: Directory containing the scene file(s) (~ expanded).

projectDir.description: The .spatialproject dir, if applicable (-p).

assertPhysics.description: If true, fail when no cooked collisionshape is produced.

toolsFull.name: generate_lighting_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneLighting.kt — an AAA lighting rig: a shadow-CASTING directional 'sun' (castsShadowEnabled + ShadowProjectionType.Auto), a cool FILL directional (no shadow, lifts shadow sides), and an EnvironmentLightingSettingsComponent IBL. Call SceneLighting.apply(content) after building the scene root, and SceneLighting.groundShadow(entity) on each 3D prop so it casts a contact shadow (a floor plane with GroundShadowComponent(false,true) receives). VERIFIED on the emulator: real soft directional shadows + PBR metals render (chrome/gold specular). Defaults are bright because the emulator IBL environment is DIM — do NOT rely on IBL alone. Set shadows=false for flat/UI scenes. RETURNS: raw Kotlin text (write it to the targetPath yourself).

sunLux.description: Shadow-casting sun intensity in lux (default 3500 — bright; emulator env is dim).

fillLux.description: Cool fill directional (no shadow) intensity (default 1800; 0 disables fill).

iblScale.description: Environment IBL intensity scale (default 2.5; 0 disables IBL).

shadows.description: Enable real projected shadows on the sun (default true; set false for flat/UI scenes).

toolsFull.name: generate_full_lighting_rig_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneLightingRig.kt — a FULL lighting rig (closes the 2-of-7 lighting gap): a directional sun + PointLightComponent (falloff) + SpotLightComponent (cone) + GroundShadowComponent (contact shadow) + EnvironmentLightingSettingsComponent (IBL). Call SceneLightingRig.apply(content) after the scene root. Compiles against the SDK; point falloff / spot cone / ground shadow are vision-verifiable on a baked-mesh scene via capture_frame.

objectName.description: Kotlin object name to emit (default SceneLightingRig). The AppSpec compiler passes SceneLighting so the template/wiring call `SceneLighting.apply(root)` invokes the FULL rig instead of failing to resolve.

toolsFull.name: generate_ibl_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneIBL.kt — image-based lighting (IBL) from an HDR .ktx cubemap. Two modes: 'stage' = scene-wide StageEnvironmentLightingComponent (lights ALL PBR meshes; ACTIVE only in FULL/PROGRESSIVE stage, INACTIVE in MIXED where the system real-world IBL wins) and 'local' = an ImageBasedLightComponent source entity + ImageBasedLightReceiverComponent on tagged receivers (localized reflections/lighting on chosen meshes). Compiles against the SDK; the IBL effect (reflections/ambient) is vision-verifiable on a baked-PBR/metallic mesh. VERIFIED usage for shiny metals: mode=`local` + intensityExponent~6 (the receiver REPLACES direct lighting, so crank it high for bright reflective metals). mode=`stage` DARKENS the whole scene on the emulator — avoid it. Bake the cubemap with prepare_ibl_cubemap (Filament cmgen); the shipped SystemIbl grayscale .ktx is dim and only darkens.

ktxAssetPath.description: Safe APK-relative path to the cubemap .ktx under app assets (loaded FROM_ASSETS), e.g. 'ibl/studio.ktx'. Only .ktx cubemaps are supported by the SDK.

mode.description: stage = scene-wide (FULL/PROGRESSIVE stage only). local = source+receiver on tagged meshes. both = emit both. Default 'stage'.

intensityExponent.description: IBL intensity exponent; actual intensity = 2^exp (range -24..24). Default 0 (= 1.0x).

toolsFull.name: generate_mr_app
toolsFull.description: Emit the proven MIXED-STAGE config (manifest pico.spatial.stage.style=1) that renders the PICO home environment + spatial content together with no falling-out, plus a minimal HomeStage.kt template (SpatialView + scene root + AgentBridge.attachScene hook). Vision-verified config (spatialdemo renders home-env + pins). NOTE (v32): scaffold_spatial_app now does Mixed natively by default (stageStyle '1'), so a new project needs no extra step — this tool remains the standalone recipe reference for the manifest block + HomeStage entry point (e.g. when retrofitting an existing app).

toolsFull.name: verify_baseline
toolsFull.description: Deterministic single-frame visual regression check. mode=save captures a baseline frame at the current camera pose; mode=check re-captures + diffs (ImageMagick MAE) and flags a REGRESSION if diff>threshold. Deterministic ONLY if the camera is unmoved between save and check (capture_frame is byte-stable when static). Returns the current frame to LOOK at. For whole-scene use verify_visual.

mode.description: save = store baseline at current pose; check = compare current frame to it.

serial.description: adb serial (default emulator-5554).

toolsFull.name: generate_spatial_audio_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SpatialAudio.kt: attach a 3D positional audio source (ObjectAudioComponent — volume + spatial radius) to an entity. Component attach is structural (logcat-assertable); audio PLAYBACK is headset-only (no guaranteed emulator audio device). Load the clip via the editor SpatialAudioFile / AudioResourceLibraryComponent.

toolsFull.name: generate_animation_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneAnimation.kt: load an AnimationResource from the bundle and play it on an entity (Entity.playAnimation -> AnimationPlaybackController), with a simple loop helper. CAVEAT (v8.1): AnimationResource playback does NOT reliably propagate through the SpatialView hierarchy for RUNTIME-built entities — expect NO visible motion there. Use this only for editor-authored/baked animation on loaded assets; for procedural motion on runtime entities use `generate_scene_animator_kotlin` (SceneAnimator, the vision-verified path). Loading/attach is structural.

toolsFull.name: generate_persistent_anchor_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit WorldAnchors.kt: create/load/remove persistent WorldAnchor poses across launches via WorldTrackingManager. Compiles + runs, but the EMULATOR has no world-tracking (createAnchor/loadAnchor return errors there) — real anchoring + cross-launch persistence are HEADSET-ONLY (C1). Persist returned UUIDs to reload.

toolsFull.name: generate_headset_readiness_codegen
toolsFull.description: Emit HeadsetReadiness.kt — a guarded registry for hardware-sensitive C1/C3/C4 initializers. Plane/mesh scene understanding can use the emulator's simulated room; controller, persistence, and physical-room conclusions remain hardware-gated. Unsupported initializers log and skip rather than crashing. Returns the Kotlin plus a manifest that separates simulator evidence from Swan obligations.

toolsFull.name: generate_hand_input_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit HandPinchInput.kt — a HEADSET-ONLY (C3) hand-pinch input registry for the HeadsetReadiness guarded-init pattern. Every SDK symbol is vault-confirmed (com.pico.spatial.tracking.hand: HandTrackingProvider/HandTrackingData/HandPose/HandJoint.Index; DataProvider start/stop/addListener) — there is NO SDK 'pinch' API, so the pinch is DERIVED as thumb-tip↔index-tip distance, the same detection generate_game_menu_kotlin's handInput path emits. On the emulator HandTrackingProvider supplies no hands: start() logs a marker and no pinches ever fire (honest no-op) — the feature is UNVERIFIABLE there; record it built_for_headset and close it via swan_verify_matrix + a device_verified entry on real hardware. Not compile-verified standalone in this repo yet (the sibling GameMenuHandInput pattern is what it mirrors); run a gradle build after wiring.

toolsFull.name: swan_bring_up_checklist
toolsFull.description: Emit a keyed PICO Swan bring-up checklist (markdown): for each headset-only feature, the exact on-hardware re-test so day-one-on-Swan is a verification pass, not a build. Feed it the headset-feature manifest from generate_headset_readiness_codegen + the capability_report builtForHeadset bucket.

ceiling.description: C1/C3/C4 (the ledger's C4_headset_only / C0_emulator spellings are normalized).

retest.description: How to verify it on Swan.

features.description: Headset-only features to re-test on hardware.

toolsFull.name: deploy_to_device
toolsFull.description: Deploy + sanity-verify on a PICO Swan HEADSET over USB (the hardware handoff).
