Every online non-emulator candidate is identity-probed: phones, Quest, and emulator-over-TCP are refused; multiple PICO-shaped devices require deviceSerial. There is no identity override. When the gate passes it installs, launches, and captures a first shell-composite frame for a later LOOK. This path has not been exercised on Swan hardware.

apkPath.description: Path to the built .apk to deploy.

deviceSerial.description: Explicit online adb serial. Required when more than one PICO-shaped candidate is attached; unrecognized identities are refused.

toolsFull.name: generate_home_env_proxy
toolsFull.description: LEGACY fixed-room proxy for an app that cannot use an open Stage: returns estimated invisible floor/bed/wall box colliders for the PICO default bedroom. Prefer generate_scene_understanding_kotlin whenever possible; emulator runtime probes measured roughly 43 simulated semantic planes and 42–44 mesh anchors. This proxy is not native scene understanding and must be calibrated by capture→LOOK→adjust.

toolsFull.name: calibrate_home_env
toolsFull.description: Vision-calibrate the LEGACY fixed-room proxy when an app cannot use native scene understanding. An open emulator Stage now exposes simulated plane/mesh geometry and is the preferred measured lane. This fallback returns six proxy faces with probe positions, a per-face looked/not-looked confidence map, and an adjusted box from caller-supplied visual deltas; it does not claim those estimates are runtime scene measurements.

room.description: Override the current proxy room box (defaults to the generate_home_env_proxy calibration: halfW 2.8, height 2.6, halfD 2.8, centerZ -1.2, thickness 0.12).

status.description: ok = marker sits ON the visible surface. too-far = the real surface is BEYOND the marker (marker floats in front of it) → grow. too-close = the surface is NEARER (marker is past/behind it) → shrink.

deltaMeters.description: How far to move this face along its outward normal (default 0.25 for too-far, -0.25 for too-close; sign auto-applied from status if omitted).

observations.description: Per-face vision observations from the capture→LOOK step. Drives the proposed room adjustment + tags faces vision-verified.

verifiedFaces.description: Faces already vision-confirmed in prior iterations (carries calibration state across stateless calls; floor is always verified).

probeInset.description: How far inside a face to place its probe marker so it visibly rests on the surface (default 0.04m).

toolsFull.name: select_home_environment
toolsFull.description: Rank measured PICO Emulator 6.0 home environments, optionally perform one guarded host selection, and report success only after a changed receipt-bound mesh uniquely classifies as the target. Scene ID and host clicks are non-discriminating; evidence ceiling is structural.

toolsFull.name: generate_particle_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneParticles.kt — a DRIVER for an editor-authored particle effect. ParticleComponent has NO public constructor (the emitter shape/rate/lifetime are authored in the Spatial Editor and baked into an AssetBundle/.glb, which auto-attaches the component); this code retrieves it via emitter.components.get<ParticleComponent>() and drives the runtime knobs: isEmitting (start/stop), startColor (constant or random range), and the attractor/vortex forces. Compiles against the SDK. ASSET-GATED: you must load an editor-authored particle node first; toggling emission/color is then vision-verifiable across captures (the forces are subtle/structural).

randomColor.description: If true, startColor varies per-particle between startColor and rangeColor (ParticleVaryingPropertyType.RANDOM); else CONSTANT. Default false.

rangeColor.description: The second color bound for RANDOM spawn color (default magenta [1,0,1,1]).

attractorStrength.description: If > 0, enables the attractor force (pulls particles toward a point) with this strength. Must be >= 0.

vortexStrength.description: If > 0, enables the vortex force (rotates particles) with this strength. Must be >= 0.

toolsFull.name: generate_video_player_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneVideo.kt — render a video onto a quad via VideoPlayerComponent + the SDK's CypressMediaPlayer. Builds a plane MeshResource + a VideoMaterial, wires the player callbacks (play on onPrepared), and attaches the component. Compiles against the SDK. ASSET + CODEC gated: needs a real video file/URL reachable via setDataSource (storage path or URL — NOT android assets, use the AssetFileDescriptor overload for bundled assets) and a hardware decoder; on the native emulator decode often fails (onError ERROR_DECODER) — the reliable signal is the logcat callbacks (onPrepared/onStarted), which is STRUCTURAL not pixel.

stereo.description: Treat the source as side-by-side stereo (VideoDimensionMode.SIDE_BY_SIDE + DisplayMode.STEREO). Default false (MONO).

toolsFull.name: generate_tween_animation_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneTween.kt — a programmatic from→to TWEEN that moves/scales/rotates an entity over time (TweenAnimation.createTweenAnimation → AnimationResource.generateWithTweenAnimation → entity.playAnimation). Supports position/scale (Vector3) and rotation (EulerAngles), ease + repeat (none/restart/reverse) + infinite loop. Compiles against the SDK; CAVEAT (v8.1/v9.6): AnimationResource/entity.playAnimation does NOT reliably propagate to RUNTIME-built entities or through a loaded model's node hierarchy — an agent animating runtime spheres/boxes/models with this gets NO visible motion. For runtime entities use `generate_scene_animator_kotlin` (SceneAnimator coroutine frame-loop — the vision-verified path); reserve this tool for editor-authored/baked animation clips.

property.description: What to animate. position/scale use [x,y,z] meters/factor; rotation uses [x,y,z] euler degrees. Default position.

repeat.description: Repeat mode (default reverse — bobs back and forth).

toolsFull.name: generate_orbit_animation_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneOrbit.kt — an ORBIT animation: an entity revolves around an axis (OrbitAnimation.createOrbitAnimation → AnimationResource.generate → entity.playAnimation). The orbit radius is the perpendicular distance of startPosition from the axis (a startPosition ON the axis gives radius 0 = no motion). Compiles against the SDK. CAVEAT (v8.1/v9.6): AnimationResource does NOT reliably propagate to RUNTIME-built entities — for runtime entities use `generate_scene_animator_kotlin` (SceneAnimator.orbit, the vision-verified path); reserve this for editor-authored/baked clips.

axis.description: Orbit axis [x,y,z] (default [0,1,0] = world up). Normalized internally; never [0,0,0].

startPosition.description: The orbiting entity's start position [x,y,z]; its perpendicular distance from the axis is the radius (default [0.6,1.2,-2.5]).

orientToPath.description: Rotate the entity to face the travel direction (default true).

toolsFull.name: generate_scene_animator_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneAnimator.kt — a RELIABLE frame-based animation driver (a coroutine loop that updates TransformComponents on the main thread each frame). Use this instead of the SDK Tween/Orbit when animating RUNTIME-built entities (spheres, boxes, models): the SDK AnimationResource does not reliably propagate through the SpatialView node hierarchy, but this per-frame TransformComponent update does (VISION-VERIFIED on the emulator: an orrery of 4 planets orbited a sun, MAE-confirmed motion). Register anims (orbit/spin/bob + material FX: pulseEmissive/fadeOpacity/cycleHue for energy/hologram/color-shift looks) after building the scene, then drive it from Compose: `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { SceneAnimator.run() }`. Returns the drop-in Kotlin.

toolsFull.name: generate_display_controllers_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneDisplay.kt — display-control helpers: OpacityControllerComponent (hierarchical fade 0..1), LookAtComponent billboarding (face the viewer/HMD or another entity, with forward-axis + up-align), and DrawOrderGroupComponent (explicit render layering for overlapping renderables). Compiles against the SDK. Opacity + draw-order + entity-target billboarding are vision-verifiable on the emulator; viewer-target billboarding faces the HMD (decoupled from the free cam, C2) so verify that mode on the headset.

forwardDirection.description: Which local axis LookAt treats as 'forward' (default NEGATIVE_Z — correct for most quads/text).

toolsFull.name: generate_portal_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit ScenePortal.kt — a portal window that renders a nested world (PortalWorldComponent root) seen through a quad with a PortalMaterial + PortalComponent. Pass a quad MeshResource for the window and a lambda that populates the nested world; the helper enforces the topology rule (portal is a SIBLING of the world, never its child). Compiles against the SDK; the portal window + nested world are vision-verifiable (aim the cam at the forward face). Entity-crossing and PASSTHROUGH background are headset-only.

doubleSide.description: Render the portal from both sides (default false — aim the cam at the forward face).

toolsFull.name: generate_rigidbody_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit ScenePhysics.kt — REAL rigid-body dynamics, VERIFIED SIMULATING ON THE EMULATOR (a launched ball strikes pins that fly — vision-verified v8.8). PhysicsWorldComponent on the scene root; STATIC colliders (box/sphere/capsule — no RigidBody, they never move); DYNAMIC bodies (box/sphere/capsule) that fall, rest, roll and collide. launch() = the safe throw (cm nudge + velocity; fires on the NEXT ~2s engine epoch — expect a beat). resetWorld() = the ONLY reliable reset (disable the old root + rebuild fresh ~3s later; destroying a physics world poisons later worlds, and per-entity destroy+respawn loses collision pairing). Keep DISCRETE collision (CONTINUOUS kills dynamic-vs-dynamic contacts); never teleport live bodies beyond a few cm (jump/timestep becomes velocity). Create every body with ALL components in one batch — the emitted helpers do. Give bodies a ModelComponent to SEE the motion; verify via frames (read-backs lag ~2s). RETURNS: raw Kotlin text (write it to the targetPath yourself).

gravity.description: World gravity [x,y,z] m/s² (default [0,-9.81,0]). Pass [0,0,0] for zero-g.

restitution.description: Default bounciness 0..1 for the physics material (default 0.2).

toolsFull.name: generate_anchor_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneAnchor.kt — AnchorComponent helpers to tether an entity to the HMD camera (createCameraTarget) or a persisted world anchor (createWorldAnchorTarget(uuid)), with position/rotation offsets and a tracking mode. Compiles against the SDK. HEADSET-ONLY (C1): anchoring is effective only in full space — it NO-OPS on the emulator (world-tracking returns nothing). Use this for Swan; verify the chain compiles + the component attaches (structural) on the emulator.

trackingMode.description: CONTINUOUS = keep following the target; ONCE = snap once. Default CONTINUOUS.

toolsFull.name: generate_game_menu_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit GameMenu.kt — a REAL in-world game menu (start/pause/resume/reset or custom buttons) with an AAA 3D feel, the way menuxr-native verified it. You provide a VERTICAL baked textured panel (bake_textured_model of a +90°X-rotated plane — see the usage note) and a list of AnimationPlaybackControllers; the menu adds a LIT 3D backing slab (depth/frame), a point light (pop), a gentle idle-bob float, and — per button — a RAISED GLASSY 3D CAP (rounded createBox) so the panel reads as real raised buttons. select(action) lifts the active cap, slides a glowing underline + cursor to the row, and PLAYS A REAL BUTTON-PRESS ANIMATION: the cap PLUNGES in and springs back (a position TweenAnimation, EASE_OUT, REVERSE×1) with a quick ripple flash (an opacity tween) — not a flat colour wash. select(action) is one entry point driven by a DEBUG_CMD broadcast on the emulator (no controller, C3) and by gaze/controller on a headset. Selection alignment + the raised cap are VISION-verifiable; pause/resume freezing is structurally verifiable via the Agent Bridge dump_scene. RETURNS: raw Kotlin text.

panelModelName.description: Baked panel model name loaded via Entity.loadSuspend (default "menu" — i.e. menu.bundle from bake_textured_model).

panelPosition.description: Panel world position [x,y,z] (default [0.85,1.45,-2.0] = to the right at eye level).

panelScale.description: Uniform panel scale (default 0.85). Children inherit it, so highlight/cursor/slab sizes are in the same panel-local units as the panel mesh.

planeHeight.description: The panel quad's full height in mesh units before scale (default 0.755 = a 900x680 texture's 680/900 aspect). Half of this is the panel half-height used for the Y formula.

textureHeight.description: Panel texture height in px (default 680). Used with rowPx to compute each button's panel-local Y.

buttons.description: Buttons as {action, rowPx} where rowPx is the button row CENTER in the texture (top=0). Default the verified 4: start@205, pause@315, resume@425, reset@535. Action names start/pause/resume/reset get built-in controller behavior; any other name calls a customActions[name] lambda.

highlightOpacity.description: Peak opacity of the ripple flash that pulses on press (default 0.6).

cursorX.description: Panel-local X of the cursor marker (default -0.36 = left end of the button row).

backingSlab.description: Add a LIT beveled 3D backing slab behind the face for depth/frame (default true = AAA).

pointLight.description: Add a point light in front of the panel so the slab catches specular (default true).

idleBob.description: Gently float the whole panel with a position tween (default FALSE — a still panel reads as firmly anchored in space, and the bob is auto-stopped the moment you move the panel anyway). Set true for the floating look.

handInput.description: Also emit GameMenuHandInput — a HEADSET-ONLY hand-tracking path: a PINCH (thumb-tip↔index-tip) near a button pokes GameMenu.select. Default false. Compiles against the tracking module but is UNVERIFIABLE on the emulator (HandTrackingProvider returns no hands — C1). Call GameMenuHandInput.start() after attach.

faceUser.description: Auto-orient the panel to FACE the user as it moves (billboard: yaw to turn toward you + pitch to tilt up/down) so it reads as a real 3D object, not a flat plane sliding on X/Y. Default true. The tilt is GENTLE + CLAMPED to ~12° (FACE_STRENGTH 0.5) so the emulator's vision-based click bridge still detects the buttons — a full face-the-user billboard slants them too far to click. On a headset (clicked by gaze/controller, not vision) you can raise FACE_STRENGTH/MAX_TILT. Recomputed on every nudgePanel + snap.

snapGrid.description: Grid size (metres) the panel snaps to when you drop it (bridge sends move:snap on release) for clean placement. Default 0.1. Set 0 to disable snapping.

toolsFull.name: mouse_bridge_start
toolsFull.description: Start the in-world-menu MOUSE BRIDGE as a DETACHED background process (idempotent — a live bridge is reused). No terminal needed: this is the baked-in replacement for manually running `pico-bridge`. The bridge lets a Mac mouse click/hover the in-world GameMenu on the emulator, auto-targeting the foreground app. fleet_build auto-calls this after launching a menu app (opt out: PICO_MCP_NO_AUTOBRIDGE=1). One-time macOS grant: Input Monitoring for the app hosting this MCP. Logs: ~/.pico-mcp/bridge.log.

hover.description: Hover preview (default ON): mousing over a button broadcasts hover:<action>. false = click-only.

packageName.description: Pin the target package. Default: auto-target the foreground spatial app (recommended).

toolsFull.name: mouse_bridge_stop
toolsFull.description: Stop the detached mouse bridge (SIGTERM the pidfile process; cleans up ~/.pico-mcp/bridge.pid).

toolsFull.name: mouse_bridge_status
toolsFull.description: Is the detached mouse bridge running? Returns pid + the last log lines (the place to see permission errors).

toolsFull.name: setup_mouse_bridge
toolsFull.description: Set up + explain the HOST MOUSE BRIDGE so the user can SELECT the in-world game menu with their Mac mouse on the emulator (there is no controller/gaze pointer on the emulator — C3). Creates the isolated venv the bridge needs (pyobjc Quartz + Pillow), best-effort checks that a menu is currently detectable on screen, and returns the exact `live` command to run plus the one-time Input Monitoring permission step. The bridge watches the real mouse over the emulator window, maps the cursor into the framebuffer, detects which menu row it is over (scene-color robust via the blue panel bbox), and on a LEFT-CLICK broadcasts <pkg>.DEBUG_CMD so GameMenu.select fires — VERIFIED end-to-end (a real click on PAUSE moved the in-world highlight to PAUSE). macOS only.

packageName.description: App package to drive, e.g. com.fleet.knockdown. If omitted, the bridge auto-detects the foreground spatial app at click time (system packages are excluded).

enableHover.description: Also PREVIEW the button under the pointer (mouse-over highlight), not just click-to-select. Apps built by generate_game_menu_kotlin route it to GameMenu.hover(); the bridge broadcasts hover:<action> only when the hovered row CHANGES (efficient). Hover never commits — a click does. Off by default.

toolsFull.name: install_bridge_launcher
toolsFull.description: Preload a project with PICO dev-convenience scripts so the mouse bridge (and a reliable emulator redeploy) are ONE CLICK in Android Studio — no more pasting the long python command. Writes pico-bridge.sh (launcher, hover-preview on by default), redeploy.sh (assemble + force-stop other spatial apps + install + launch), Android Studio run configs (.run/*.run.xml → green ▶ 'Mouse Bridge' / 'Redeploy (emulator)'), and a pico.gradle.kts wired into the root build (Gradle tool window > pico > mouseBridge / redeploy). Idempotent. scaffold_spatial_app runs this automatically for new projects; use this tool to add it to existing ones. macOS.

projectDir.description: The Android project root (e.g. ~/AndroidStudioProjects/menuxr-native).

toolsFull.name: generate_layout_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneLayout.kt — an ANALYTICAL spatial layout engine that positions N content entities in a pattern (WALL row / GRID / ARC facing the viewer / SHELF stacked rows). You supply a factory `(index) -> Entity` that returns the content (a baked card/model/quad); SceneLayout computes each slot's position + facing yaw and parents it under the scene root. Positions are derived from geometry (never eyeballed — the retained game-menu lesson). All params are runtime-mutable vars (defaults baked from these inputs) so a data-driven count or a vision-calibration pass can override without regen. Compiles against SDK 0.13.3; the arrangement is vision-verifiable (aim the cam at centerZ and LOOK — C2). RETURNS: raw Kotlin text (write it to the targetPath yourself).

pattern.description: Default layout pattern (default 'arc'). Runtime-overridable per place() call.

count.description: Default item count used by convenience helpers (default 6). place() takes an explicit count.

radius.description: ARC radius in meters from the viewer (default 2.5).

spacing.description: Gap between items in meters for WALL/GRID/SHELF (default 0.6).

centerY.description: Vertical center / eye height in meters (default 1.4).

centerZ.description: Forward distance in meters for WALL/GRID/SHELF, negative = in front (default -2.5).

arcSpanDeg.description: Total angular span of the ARC in degrees (default 90).

faceUser.description: If true (default), each ARC item is yawed to face the viewer at the origin.

yawOffsetDeg.description: Extra yaw added to every faced item (default 0) — the vision-calibration knob for the plane-facing convention.

toolsFull.name: generate_interaction_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneInteraction.kt — a raycast-driven selection/hover engine for spatial objects. register(id, entity, ...) marks an object interactable (InteractableComponent + a primitive box CollisionComponent so a ray can hit it) and stores its onSelect/onHover callbacks; select(id)/hover(id) are the BROADCAST entry points (C0, emulator-verifiable via <pkg>.DEBUG_CMD) and pick(scene, origin, dir) is the RAY entry point (gaze-dwell/controller-ray — real only on Swan, C3). Tracks selection state and applies an optional scale-bump highlight (scaleVector — a same-scale highlight is invisible, the retained lesson). Requires a PhysicsWorldComponent on an ancestor for the ray path (use SpatialColliders.attachPhysicsWorld from generate_collider_kotlin). Compiles against SDK 0.13.3; broadcast-select + highlight are vision-verifiable on the emulator, controller-ray is built-for-Swan. RETURNS: raw Kotlin text (write it to the targetPath yourself).

highlightScale.description: Scale multiplier applied to the selected item (default 1.1). Set 1.0 to disable the scale highlight.

defaultBoxSize.description: Default interactable collider FULL box size [x,y,z] in meters (default [0.6,0.6,0.04]). createBox uses FULL extents.

toolsFull.name: generate_tappable_detail_kotlin

toolsFull.name: perf_diagnose
toolsFull.description: Run PICO's OFFICIAL performance profiler (`pico-cli perf live run`) against a running app for a fixed window and return its validated JSON report: app/system FPS percentiles, CPU/GPU usage, jank windows, and pico-cli's DIAGNOSIS (bottleneck category + rule + evidence — e.g. INSUFFICIENT_DATA, APP, SPR). Prefer this over measure_perf for engine/3D-pipeline analysis; keep measure_perf for the 2D UI-frame (gfxinfo) view. Dispatch requires verified `perf live run` capability evidence for the resolved package: an unprovisioned or environment-gated profiler is refused with the CLI's own reason and the retained evidence paths, and this server never sets PICO_HOME and never runs setup. The report is validated before it is reported — its package identity must match the request, its schema must be a published one (reportVersion 0.2.0/0.1.0), and a report file that predates the run is refused. The result reports `requestedDevice` — the explicit `device` you named or the default this wrapper substituted — so a report is never read against the wrong target. Read `measurement` before reading any number: 'missing' (including the profiler's own SKIP/INSUFFICIENT_DATA) is NOT a pass, and Spatial Runtime FPS never stands in for app FPS. Resolves the latest managed @picoxr/pico-cli lazily on first use and runs its absolute path; successful resolution is reported in picoCli provenance. Failures carry an honest failureClass for managed policy/freshness, setup-required, environment, flag-or-version-drift (the CLI rejected our flags), or runtime (read the CLI's outputTail — the cause is not guessed for you). The full raw report is saved to reportPath for deep dives. HONESTY: All metrics are real pico-cli measurements; absent counters arrive as 0/absent — on the emulator GPU counters are typically unparseable, so gpu* zeros mean 'not measured', never 'GPU idle'. The diagnosis block is pico-cli's own rule engine quoted verbatim (rule + evidence included). measurement says how much was actually measured: 'missing' (including the profiler's own SKIP/INSUFFICIENT_DATA) is never a pass, and Spatial Runtime FPS never stands in for app FPS. Evidence class: structural — not a substitute for LOOKING at a capture.

toolsFull.name: perf_trace
toolsFull.description: Drive PICO's OFFICIAL Perfetto trace pipeline (`pico-cli perf trace`) — the real 3D frame-pacing evidence that gfxinfo/measure_perf cannot see. action='record' traces the device for durationSec (bounded — the CLI's Ctrl+C live mode is not wrapped) and returns the .perfetto-trace path; 'decode' converts a trace to json/systrace/ctrace (may auto-download traceconv on first use); 'load' starts a trace_processor session and returns its sessionId from the profiler's VALIDATED JSON envelope (sessionSource says whether it came from the envelope or the legacy `[TraceLoad] Session:` label); 'query' runs SQL against a loaded session and returns the envelope's data.rows — never the envelope itself, and an empty rows array is a real answer. Dispatch requires verified capability evidence for the exact trace route on the resolved package; an unprovisioned or environment-gated profiler is refused without running anything, and this server never sets PICO_HOME and never runs setup. Bounded raw stdout/stderr are retained immutably (retainedLog). Resolves the latest managed @picoxr/pico-cli lazily and runs its absolute path. Failures carry an honest managed policy/freshness, flag-or-version-drift, setup-required (returning an absolute manual setupCommand), environment, or runtime failureClass with the CLI's own outputTail. HONESTY: Everything returned is pico-cli's own output (verbatim tail) plus stat-checked artifact paths; raw stdout/stderr are retained immutably. Session ids and query rows come from the profiler's validated JSON envelope (success/resource/action/session checked before anything is unwrapped) — never scraped from prose, and an empty rows array is a real answer, not a missing one. The flag surface was read from the vendored profiler package's own declarations (0.1.0 on the 0.4.x line, 0.2.0 on 0.5.x); an end-to-end record on a device is not ledgered. Evidence class: structural — trace numbers are not a substitute for LOOKING at frames.

toolsFull.name: watch_crash
toolsFull.description: Monitor a package for crashes with PICO's OFFICIAL crash watcher (`pico-cli app watch-crash <pkg>`: PID-change polling + surfaced exception logs) for a bounded window. On a CLI line whose retained help advertises `--monitor-timeout` the requested window is handed to the CLI itself; on a line without it the CLI's own monitoring bound is a constant this wrapper cannot set. Either way an outer watchdog kills a stuck child after the requested window — plus 20s of settlement grace only where the CLI was given that window — reported as endedBy:'duration-cap …'. watchedSec is the OBSERVED elapsed window, never the requested one — read observation.coverage (complete/partial/unknown) and assessment before treating a quiet window as a no-crash result. Bounded raw stdout/stderr are retained immutably (retainedLog) and the crash scan reads that complete log, not the returned tail. Requires an explicit `device` serial — there is no default target, and a missing one is refused before any CLI resolution. Optionally starts the app first (--start/--activity); nothing is launched implicitly. Dispatch requires verified `app watch-crash` capability evidence for the resolved package. Resolves the latest managed @picoxr/pico-cli lazily and runs its absolute path; successful resolution is returned as picoCli provenance. HONESTY: watchedSec is the OBSERVED elapsed window, never the requested one; requestedDurationSec and observation.coverage say how much of the request was actually covered. On a line that advertises --monitor-timeout the request is handed to the CLI; otherwise the CLI's own monitoring bound is a constant this wrapper did not set and an outer watchdog only bounds a stuck child. monitoredSec is null: neither retained pico-cli line reports how long it monitored after paying for device resolution, the optional launch and the PID wait out of the same budget, so elapsed wall-clock time must not be read as monitoring time. crashIndicated is a best-effort keyword scan over the complete retained log (not just the returned tail) — read outputTail and the retained log before claiming a crash or its absence; unless coverage is 'complete', a quiet window is 'inconclusive', not a no-crash result. Evidence class: structural.

toolsFull.name: capture_record
toolsFull.description: Record the device screen with PICO's OFFICIAL recorder (`pico-cli capture record`, 1-180s) and pull the file locally as a RECORDING evidence artifact — the video lane for demos and ledger evidence that single-frame captures lack. Returns the stat-checked output path + size. Resolves the latest managed @picoxr/pico-cli lazily and runs its absolute path; successful resolution is returned as picoCli provenance. READ `status` AND `media` TOGETHER: `status` grades the recording CALL (ok = the CLI exited 0, the file exists with real bytes, and container inspection did not fail); `media` is the separate validation verdict — validated = the container parsed, invalid = it did not (status is then failed), unvalidated = the container was NOT inspected at all (over the inspection budget, or unreadable), so status ok with media unvalidated is an uninspected file, never a validated recording. HONESTY: The artifact is the file pulled by the official CLI. This tool stat-checks it AND inspects its container: box structure, declared tracks, and the duration MEASURED from the file's own movie header. A returned duration is NOT a measurement — the CLI echoes the clamped request, so requestedDurationSec and measuredDurationSec are reported separately and may disagree. A container that will not parse is invalid media; when nothing could inspect the bytes the media is unvalidated, never a successful decode. Its pixels still prove nothing until LOOKED at. Guest-side adb screenrecord and pico-cli capture record yield empty/invalid files on this emulator display; the working macOS host-side recipe is screencapture -V -l<windowId>. Evidence class: a capture artifact that still requires a LOOK before any visual claim.

durationSec.description: Recording length in seconds (CLI range 1-180; default 15).

device.description: REQUIRED adb device serial. There is no default: a recording names the device it came from.

outputPath.description: Local output path. Default: a run-unique file under the observation root, never a fixed or shared path a later recording can overwrite.

status.description: Grades the recording CALL only: ok = the CLI exited 0, the recording exists with real bytes (stat-checked — exit 0 alone is never ok) and container inspection did not fail; failed = run failed, the file is missing/empty, or the container is invalid; unavailable = pico-cli absent/unusable. Read `media` for whether the container was actually validated.

failureClass.description: Why the CLI lane failed: managed policy/freshness, setup-required, flag/version drift, or runtime.

note.description: This wrapper's guidance in plain words — remedies included, causes never guessed.

outputTail.description: The CLI's own words (verbatim tail) — read before assuming a cause.

outputTruncated.description: True when CLI output exceeded the capture cap; scans over it are partial.

honesty.description: The wrapper's standing honesty contract for this result.

picoCli.description: Managed/external CLI identity and freshness provenance for every successful ensure-backed result.

setupCommand.description: Absolute manual setup guidance. This server never executes it.

artifact.description: The recording path. Its pixels prove nothing until LOOKED at.

durationSec.description: Deprecated alias of requestedDurationSec — the CLAMPED REQUEST, never a measurement.

requestedDurationSec.description: What this wrapper asked the CLI for, after clamping to the 1-180s range.

measuredDurationSec.description: Duration read from the recording's OWN movie header. null when the container states none or nothing could inspect it.

media.description: The validation verdict, separate from `status`: validated = the container parsed; invalid = it did not (status is then failed); unvalidated = the container was NOT inspected (over the inspection budget, or unreadable) — never a successful decode, so status ok beside it means an uninspected file.

toolsFull.name: resolve_semantic_placement
toolsFull.description: Resolve a LABEL-ANCHORED placement against a scanned world's semantic scene (semantic_splat_scan -> compose_semantic_scene): given labeled 3D boxes and an anchor like {label:'counter', relation:'on-top-of'}, returns the concrete world position for the child content, with fuzzy label matching + ambiguity reporting. Relations: on-top-of (stack on the box top), next-to (step out along the object's free side), in-front-of (toward the room center), plus offset/gap tuning. This is what lets an AppSpec object say anchorTo:{label} and land on a REAL surface by name (the compiler calls the same resolver). HONESTY: pure geometry over labeled boxes — structural evidence; visually verify the placement inside the world before claiming it.

label.description: Target object by name, e.g. 'counter', 'neon menu'.

childSize.description: Full extents of the content being placed (default 0.3m cube).

floorY.description: Floor Y from the scan (grounds next-to / in-front-of).

bounds.description: Room bounds (gives in-front-of its 'toward the room' direction).

toolsFull.name: calibrate_capture_camera
toolsFull.description: Solve the emulator forward-capture camera model EMPIRICALLY from a capture of color-keyed cubes at KNOWN app-space positions (build briefs/calib.json via fleet_build first). Detects each cube's pixel centroid (saturation-keyed), solves focal length from the horizontal offsets and eye height from the verticals (least squares), reports per-marker residuals, and persists ~/.pico-mcp/camera-calibration.json for measure_placement. HONESTY: residuals are stored and echoed into every later measurement; recalibrate after any emulator/renderer update AND after every emulator cold restart — the v24 run measured a 299px cy shift across one restart (the free-cam default pose moved), which silently corrupts every meter figure until recalibration.

markers.description: At least 3 markers; include off-center x AND differing y for a solvable system.

toolsFull.name: measure_placement
toolsFull.description: MEASURE a placement instead of just looking: detect color-keyed content in a deterministic forward capture, project its EXPECTED world position through the calibrated camera (calibrate_capture_camera first), and report the error in pixels and meters-at-depth, plus IoU between the detected pixels and the projected expected 3D box. This is the ledger's error bar: attach the returned numbers to a vision_verified record. Targets behind the eye or off-frame are reported as such, never guessed.

expectedPosition.description: Where the pipeline placed it (app space).

toolsFull.name: critique_capture
toolsFull.description: Turn a LOOKED-at capture into a structured defect list that feeds replan_spec (the v5.2 self-repair loop). You still do the seeing (ground-truth rule): pass what you observed as `observations` and this maps each to a defect with a diagnose/replan SYMPTOM + DESIGN.md rule + suggested fix, and returns `replanFailures` ready for replan_spec. It also runs cheap pixel heuristics (mean brightness, non-black coverage, dominant colors) as ASSISTS and returns the DESIGN.md rubric to judge against. If you pass `expected` (minObjects/notMostlyBlack/colorsPresent) it adds heuristic defects (e.g. mostly-black → not_rendering). Capture → LOOK → critique_capture → replan_spec → recompile the failed subtree.

claim.description: What the frame should show, e.g. '6 shelf cards render lit in the forward FOV'.

imagePath.description: Path to the capture (adb screencap PNG) — enables the pixel heuristics.

defect.description: What's wrong, in plain words (mapped to a symptom).

targetRef.description: The spec node id the defect belongs to.

observations.description: Your visual findings. Omit to just get the rubric + heuristics.

toolsFull.name: record_verification
toolsFull.description: Append a verification claim, append an immutable retraction, or explicitly promote a native run receipt into portable one-hop provenance. Record, retract, and promote fields are mutually exclusive. Promotion publishes receipt objects only and never creates evidence. Image evidence needs a structurally complete PNG/JPEG plus attestation and is copied into content-addressed storage. To bind an exact LOOK, pass runReceiptId and, for a portable receipt, its runReceiptPromotionId; binding never changes the requested evidence class. device_verified additionally uses live identity + same-serial screencap probes. Stored bytes are revalidated on every report read.

app.description: Canonical app/package ledger key: lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen; no paths or spaces.

action.description: Default record. Retract appends a correction; promote publishes a portable one-hop receipt without ledger evidence.

claim.description: Record action: the claim, e.g. '6 shelf cards render in the forward FOV'.

evidenceType.description: Record action: how it was verified. Image-grounded classes require a linked capture + attestation. auto_judged/usd_host_render cannot be minted here; use their producer tools.

artifactPath.description: Path to the capture that was LOOKED at or measured; copied into immutable ledger-owned storage.

attestation.description: What was seen or measured (required for image-grounded evidence).

runReceiptId.description: Record action only: receiptId returned by pico_build_app. Pass it only after LOOKING at that receipt's exact capture; binding records provenance and never promotes the evidence class.

runReceiptPromotionId.description: Record action only: promotionId returned with a portable receipt. Omit it for a native receipt; portable and native kinds never fall back to one another.

deviceSerial.description: Attached adb serial (REQUIRED for device_verified; the server probes this serial live).

deviceModel.description: Optional expected ro.product.model; if supplied it must match the live probe.

deviceFingerprint.description: Optional expected ro.build.fingerprint; if supplied it must match the live probe.

deviceBootQemu.description: Optional expected ro.boot.qemu; if supplied it must match the live probe. Live value '1' is rejected.

deviceFeature.description: device_verified only: structured feature slug measured on-device (for example controller_ray); required with deviceOutcome.

deviceOutcome.description: device_verified only: explicit observed outcome. Parity closes only an exact deviceFeature with pass; claim prose is never interpreted as polarity.

targetSeq.description: Retract action: sequence of the earlier claim to correct.

retractionReason.description: Retract action: why the earlier claim can no longer be relied on.

retractionNote.description: Retract action: optional nuance retained in history.

sourceReceiptId.description: Promote action only: exact native source receipt identity.

sourceReceiptRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical native receipt-store root.

sourceLedgerRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical source ledger-store root.

targetReceiptRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical target receipt-store root.

targetLedgerRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical target ledger-store root.

toolsFull.name: ledger_report
toolsFull.description: Read an app's complete append-only trust-ledger history, honor retraction events, revalidate every linked image against its recorded hash/metadata, and generate the capability report from only effective evidence. Missing, malformed, or changed captures are explicit provenance-broken structural rows and never print as vision_verified/device_verified/auto_judged/usd_host_render.

app.description: Canonical app/package ledger key: lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen; no paths or spaces.

toolsFull.name: generate_claims_page
toolsFull.description: Generate the PUBLIC verifiable-claims snapshot from the trust ledgers. Every linked image is revalidated; unreadable ledgers are disclosed in JSON/HTML and make status incomplete rather than silently disappearing from the corpus. Emits static HTML plus claims.json. Optional filters: apps and minEvidence.

apps.description: restrict to these app packages (ledger file stems)

minEvidence.description: weakest evidence class to include (default: include all)

toolsFull.name: run_spatialbench
toolsFull.description: v23 SPATIALBENCH: score the conformance corpus (briefs/) as a public benchmark and emit a static league-table report (docs/spatialbench/). tier='headless' (default, CI-safe) scores planned/compiled/shape per brief from the spec+ledger alone — /3, no runtime claims. tier='full' additionally fleet-builds each brief on the emulator and scores booted/captured plus the stage eye when applicable. v32 adds the ADDITIVE MR tier (BENCH_MR: Mixed-stage briefs, reported as their own mrTier section) alongside the frozen BENCH_CORE; on high-coverage passthrough frames count/not-black/dominant-color checks are advisory with zero confidence, while at least two authored colors can score through the color-key lane at the default 0.8 threshold; other MR rows escalate. eye is the CALIBRATED JUDGE (auto_judged, never vision_verified; escalations name stage frames for a human LOOK). Briefs that declare panels gain a separate panelReady axis backed only by structural WindowManager caption/container evidence; it never becomes eye or vision proof. Panel-only routes leave eye null and exclude it from the maximum rather than false-failing an off-view panel. Asset-gated or explicitly external-implementation briefs are reported as skipped, not failed. perfAxis:true (tier='full' only) adds an optional perf axis: perfSource='gfxinfo' (default) scores measure_perf's UI/RenderThread p95 under perfBudgetMs — gfxinfo's UI surfaces only, not the spatial engine's 3D pacing; perfSource='pico-cli' closes that gap via the official profiler (perf_diagnose), scoring appFps p5 (the report's frame-time-p95 analog — it has no appFps p95 field) against the budget's fps floor, and falls back to gfxinfo with the reason in notes when the CLI or appFps data is absent (on this emulator appFps measures 0/no_3d_frame). Either source scores null (not counted, never zeroed) without data. Returns the report paths + the league table.

tier.description: headless = spec+ledger axes only; full = also emulator boot/capture/eye per brief (slow, serial)

briefIds.description: full tier defaults to the self-contained core set [crystals, boutique, knockdown, gallery, console, dashboard, ambient, affordance] plus the additive MR tier [mrtable, mrpedestal, mrknock]; headless defaults to every brief

settleSec.description: full tier: seconds to settle after launch before capture

perfAxis.description: tier='full' only: after boot/capture/eye, sample the perfSource for the brief's package and score a 7th 'perf' axis (0/1/null)

perfBudgetMs.description: perfAxis frame budget in ms (default 16.7ms = 60fps-class): gfxinfo verdicts the UI/RenderThread p95 against it; pico-cli verdicts appFps p5 against its fps floor (1000/budget)

perfSource.description: perfAxis source: 'gfxinfo' = measure_perf UI-frame p95 (emulator-safe default); 'pico-cli' = perf_diagnose's appFps p5 via the official profiler (real 3D pacing — the managed resolver supplies a runnable absolute path; falls back to gfxinfo, with the reason in notes, when resolution or appFps data is absent)

toolsFull.name: solve_free_placement
toolsFull.description: v24 AFFORDANCE SOLVER: find a COLLISION-FREE pose for a child object in a scanned world — 'put a 30cm bowl ON the counter, 10cm clear of everything, facing the neon sign'. Extracts support surfaces (floor + usable object tops) from the semantic scene, grid-searches free space against every other labeled box, and returns the best pose + rotationYDeg (when facing is set) + up to 3 alternatives — or an HONEST no-fit naming the tightest gap it found (never a silent overlap). visibleFrom + occupancyPath reject occluded candidates; captureFrustum additionally rejects child boxes outside the calibrated deterministic forward frame. Feed the pose into an AppSpec transform, or use anchorTo:{label, relation:'on', clearance} and the compiler routes through this solver. Structural evidence only until a frame is LOOKED at.

semanticScenePath.description: Path to a compose_semantic_scene JSON (or pass objects inline).

childSize.description: [w,h,d] meters of the thing being placed.

clearance.description: Min gap to obstacles and surface edges (default 0.05m).

avoiding.description: Labels to keep distance from (soft constraint).

occupancyPath.description: build_occupancy_grid output JSON — UNLABELED scanned geometry then also blocks candidates (closes the ramen-counter class of miss).

visibleFrom.description: v27.3 LINE OF SIGHT: a viewpoint in the app frame (e.g. the spawn camera [0,1.2,0]). Requires occupancyPath — candidates whose ray to visibleFrom is occluded by scanned geometry are hard-rejected, not just non-intersecting ones.

cx.description: Calibrated principal point X in pixels.

cy.description: Calibrated principal point Y in pixels.

captureFrustum.description: v27.7 CAPTURE FOV: calibrated deterministic-forward intrinsics. Requires visibleFrom; candidates whose projected child AABB is less than minVisibleFraction (default 0.5) inside the frame are hard-rejected.

toolsFull.name: build_occupancy_grid
toolsFull.description: OCCUPANCY FROM GEOMETRY: voxelize a splat scan (.ply/.spz) into a persistent occupancy grid so solve_free_placement avoids UNLABELED obstacles, not just detector-labeled boxes (closes the ramen-counter finding: a scanned-but-unlabeled counter occluding a 'free' placement). liftFloorToZero shifts the estimated floor band to y=0 to match the app/semantic-scene frame (the v19 world-seating recipe). Saves the grid JSON and returns stats; pass its path as occupancyPath to solve_free_placement, or set meta.occupancyPath in an AppSpec so anchorTo relation:'on' routes through it at compile time. Structural evidence only — LOOK at a frame before claiming placement.

splatPath.description: Path to the .ply or .spz splat scan.

cell.description: Voxel size in meters (default 0.05; auto-raised if the grid exceeds 8M cells).

liftFloorToZero.description: Shift the estimated floor band to y=0 — the app/semantic frame (default true).

minPointsPerCell.description: Occupancy threshold (default: mean occupied density, min 2 — drops splat mist).

toolsFull.name: live_spawn
toolsFull.description: v25 LIVE COPILOT: spawn a primitive INTO a RUNNING fleet app (Agent Bridge `spawn` over am broadcast) — no rebuild, no relaunch. Awaits the bridge's tagged ack (spawned / spawn_failed); a missing ack returns no-ack, never a silent success. Spawned entities are visual-only (no physics body). Verify with live_scene_diff and, for visual claims, capture + LOOK.

id.description: Entity name (must be unique in the scene)

dims.description: box full extents; sphere uses dims[0] as radius (default 0.3s)

toolsFull.name: live_move
toolsFull.description: v25 LIVE COPILOT: move a named entity in a RUNNING fleet app (Agent Bridge `move`). Awaits the tagged ack (moved / move_failed / no-ack). Works on any entity with a TransformComponent — including compile-time content. Do NOT live-move physics bodies (adapter rule: no runtime teleports); verify with live_scene_diff.

id.description: Entity name as shown by dump_scene

toolsFull.name: live_remove
toolsFull.description: v25 LIVE COPILOT: destroy a named entity in a RUNNING fleet app (Agent Bridge `remove`). Awaits the tagged ack (removed / remove_failed / no-ack). Do NOT remove physics bodies at runtime (adapter rule: no destroy+respawn); verify with live_scene_diff.

toolsFull.name: live_scene_snapshot
toolsFull.description: v25 LIVE COPILOT: dump the RUNNING app's scene graph (Agent Bridge dump_scene) into structured entities [{name, depth, pos, comps}]. Take one before and one after a live edit and feed both to live_scene_diff — that diff is the structural proof of what actually changed.

toolsFull.name: live_scene_diff
toolsFull.description: v25 LIVE COPILOT: diff two live_scene_snapshot entity lists (before vs after a live edit) — added / removed / moved (with per-entity delta meters). This is the copilot's verification: the RUNNING app's own testimony of what changed. Structural evidence; pair with capture + LOOK for visual claims.

toolsFull.name: vault_workspaces
toolsFull.description: v26: list the agent-vault WORKSPACES materialized on this machine (~/Library/PICO/sdk/<version>/agent-vault) — one per SDK version supplied by the CLI's separately provisioned utility payload. Feed two versions to vault_diff for a drift report; pass a version to vault_api to query that SDK's declarations.

toolsFull.name: vault_diff
toolsFull.description: v26 DRIFT REPORT: diff two agent-vault indexes (SDK versions or explicit vault roots) — types added/removed, members added/removed, constructor-arity changes, enum-entry drift, kind changes — each breaking change paired with a concrete MIGRATION HINT (the instant upgrade brief for spatial-sdk-update work). HONESTY: speaks only for what both vaults declare; renames are flagged as 'likely' only when exactly one member was removed and one added.

from.description: Source SDK version ('0.13') or an explicit agent-vault root path.

to.description: Target SDK version or vault root.

toolsFull.name: stack_new
toolsFull.description: Create an isolated git worktree + branch for a stacked change (safe parallel work — no shared-file clobber). Returns the worktree path + branch. Work in that dir, then stack_verify + stack_land.

name.description: Short kebab-case change name, e.g. 'fix-layout-arc'. Becomes branch stack/<name>.

repoDir.description: The git repo root (e.g. the pico-spatial-mcp checkout).

base.description: Base ref to branch from (default the current branch/HEAD).

toolsFull.name: stack_verify
toolsFull.description: Run a verify command inside a stacked worktree (its OWN node-verify before landing). Default 'npm run build && npm run smoke'. Returns pass/fail + output tail. (The worktree needs its own deps for smoke — pass a lighter command like 'npm run build' if node_modules aren't installed there.)

command.description: Verify command (default 'npm run build && npm run smoke').

toolsFull.name: stack_land
toolsFull.description: Land a stacked change: push its branch and (if gh is installed) open a PR onto the base — an independently-revertable link in the stack. Does NOT merge automatically (review first). Set removeWorktree to clean up the worktree after pushing.

branch.description: The branch to push, e.g. stack/fix-layout-arc.

openPr.description: Open a gh PR after pushing (default true if gh is available).

removeWorktree.description: Remove the worktree after landing (default false).

toolsFull.name: run_brief_suite
toolsFull.description: Run the brief-generality eval corpus: for each brief in briefs/ (brief + draft AppSpec + expected shape), headlessly PLAN (validate + feasibility lint) and COMPILE (build ledger), score against the expected node counts + C-class split, and emit a scorecard (planned/compiled/shape-match/verifiableNow/builtForSwan + ledger evidence counts). Positive device_verified PASS and looked-at device FAIL findings are counted separately; FAIL never contributes to lookedVerified proof. Fully headless + reproducible; per-brief emulator builds + a visual montage are the emulator-gated extension.

briefsDir.description: Directory of brief JSON files (default the repo's briefs/).

toolsFull.name: regression_gate
toolsFull.description: Block ship on any regression against committed goldens. mode='save' recomputes the brief-suite scorecard and writes briefs/golden-scorecard.json + repro.lock.json (SDK pin + canonical pose + golden AVD snapshot name). mode='check' re-runs the suite and BLOCKS if any brief regressed pass→fail or the score dropped (deterministic, headless), and — if you pass frame pairs — runs a downscaled MAE compare of each committed golden PNG vs a fresh capture (MAE is an assist: nonzero = CHANGED → LOOK at the pair; vision is the verdict). Overall verdict PASS / LOOK / BLOCK.

mode.description: save = write goldens; check = compare + gate.

canonicalPose.description: The canonical free-cam pose goldens were captured at (recorded in repro.lock).

goldenAvdSnapshot.description: Named AVD snapshot to snapshot_load before capturing goldens (the true reproducibility lock).

fresh.description: fresh capture PNG path to compare

frames.description: Golden-frame pairs to MAE-compare (emulator-gated; capture the fresh frames at the canonical pose first).

toolsFull.name: list_templates
toolsFull.description: List the 8 parameterized AppSpec skeletons (gallery / inspection / dashboard / ambient / showcase / studio / constellation / KNOCKDOWN) — the proven app shapes you can instantiate for a new brief instead of authoring from scratch. `knockdown` is the REAL-physics game (physics + clickable GameMenu + live-text scoreboard — the proof-path for physics/interactive/hybrid briefs); `studio` is AAA PBR-metal; `constellation` is ambient + SceneAnimator. Each names its params + which are data-bound/interactive + any Swan-only pieces. Instantiate with instantiate_template(name, brief, appName, packageName[, count, palette]).

toolsFull.name: instantiate_template
toolsFull.description: Instantiate a template skeleton into a concrete, validated AppSpec for a new brief — ready for plan_app_spec -> compile_app_spec. Stamps the app/package + count + palette; for data-bound templates it also returns a sample data JSON (write it to app/src/main/assets/data/items.json). Reuse over the v5.0 pipeline; the output is regression-gated like any other app.

brief.description: The new brief this instance realizes.

palette.description: Optional [r,g,b] 0..1 colors for data-bound sample items.

toolsFull.name: remix_app
toolsFull.description: Remix an existing native app to a new brief. Decodes the app (its applicationId + the content Kotlin the loop authored) into an approximate CURRENT AppSpec; if you pass a proposedSpec (the new brief's AppSpec, e.g. from instantiate_template), it returns the node-level DIFF (added/removed/changed) + the exact recompile set — so you recompile + re-verify ONLY the changed nodes, not the whole app. Reads authored content (never a bundle md5). Remember to re-grep/rename the package + keep local.properties sdk.dir + the SpatialDemo log tag; headset-only features carry their class forward.

existingProjectDir.description: Path to the existing Android project (e.g. ~/AndroidStudioProjects/showroomxr-native).

newBrief.description: The new brief to remix toward.

proposedSpec.description: Optional new-brief AppSpec (from instantiate_template/plan_app_spec). If given, returns the diff + recompile set.

toolsFull.name: generate_scene_router_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneRouter.kt — a broadcast-driven scene-graph state machine for multi-scene apps. Register each scene as a builder lambda ((container: Entity) -> Unit); go(id) tears down the current scene (Entity.destroy) and builds the target fresh under its own container (resetting per-scene state). ⚠️ PHYSICS: do NOT route a scene that owns a PhysicsWorldComponent through this — destroying a physics-world tree POISONS every physics world built later in-process (rule R3) and destroy+respawn loses collision pairing. Physics scenes: register them with SceneRouter.registerPhysics(id, builder) — go() then DISABLES (enabled=false) instead of destroying, per rule R3. Disabled physics containers accumulate (documented trade-off); non-physics scenes destroy cleanly. Drive transitions with a <pkg>.DEBUG_CMD 'navigate:<id>' broadcast (C4-safe, mouse-bridge-compatible); portal/gaze/controller activation is built-for-Swan (C3). Scene mutation is marshaled to the main thread (broadcasts arrive off-main). Compiles against SDK 0.13.3; a broadcast transition between scenes is vision-verifiable by capturing each scene individually (with ~3s settle).

toolsFull.name: generate_composition_scene
toolsFull.description: Emit a composed USDA scene that layers multiple authored sub-scenes via USD references + non-destructive `over` overrides (extends compose_scene). Each layer references a sub-scene asset with an optional translate/scale; each override targets a prim path with authored attributes. GOTCHA baked in: the Spatial Editor DROPS hand-authored `over` blocks on re-save — if this round-trips the editor, diff the USDA (never a bundle md5) and re-apply overrides. For RUNTIME scene switching prefer generate_scene_router_kotlin (broadcast-driven, C4-safe). Returns the USDA text; pack with pack_bundle and verify with inspect_bundle.

reference.description: Sub-scene asset path, e.g. scenes/lobby.usda or ../Assets/x.usdz.

layers.description: The sub-scenes to compose (referenced, not copied).

attributes.description: Raw USDA attribute lines, e.g. 'float inputs:intensity = 800'.

overrides.description: Non-destructive `over` blocks layered on top of the references.

toolsFull.name: generate_interactable_registry_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit InteractableRegistry.kt — the app self-describes its clickable interactables (id + base colour hex + layout slot) as a logcat marker (INTERACTABLES|<json>) emitted for host bridge consumers. Call add(id, colorHex, slot) as you build each card, then publish(); a consumer greps `adb logcat -s InteractableRegistry` for the JSON, maps a click's colour->id, and fires a `select:<id>` DEBUG_CMD broadcast (that broadcast route is real today, and drives generate_tappable_detail_kotlin / SceneInteraction). HONEST STATUS: the SHIPPED tools/mouse_menu_bridge.py does NOT yet read this marker — it detects only the fixed 4-colour GameMenu bars; a registry-driven bridge consumer is pending host-side work. Compiles against SDK 0.13.3; a real Mac click through the (menu) bridge was vision-verified end-to-end in v4.7.

toolsFull.name: plan_layout_and_camera
toolsFull.description: Plan an N-item layout intelligently: compute the slots (mirrors SceneLayout math), flag any that land IN THE HOME-ENV BED (so cards aren't sunk into the bed — floor y=0 is the only vision-verified anchor) with a suggested fix, and plan the emulator_look sweep verify_app_spec needs to SEE every object (azimuth span + capture count; content outside the forward FOV can't be captured, C2). Advisory poses (the free cam takes relative drags). Use before compile to size the layout + before verify to know how many capture angles to sweep.

onHomeEnv.description: If true (default), check slots against the home-env bed AABB.

toolsFull.name: import_model_catalog
toolsFull.description: Batch-bake a catalog of textured models into N distinct .bundles (via spatialbundle) and stage them in an app's assets — so a data-at-scale scene shows real distinct models, not just tinted quads. Give a modelsDir (all GLB/GLTF/USD*) or an explicit models list + the app's assetsDir; each is baked (never runtime-load a raw GLB) and verified (texture+material present). Missing sources return a dry-run PLAN (no fake bakes). Returns per-model {name, bundle, rendersTextured} + a JSON data-node stub keyed to each bundle for generate_data_binding_kotlin. Baking leaves generated assets/BundleCache/ content; exclude BundleCache from APK assets with androidResources.ignoreAssetsPattern and add app/src/main/assets/BundleCache/ to .gitignore.

models.description: Explicit model paths. Omit to scan modelsDir.

assetsDir.description: App assets dir to stage bundles into, e.g. <project>/app/src/main/assets.

dryRun.description: Plan only — don't bake (default false; auto-true if sources missing).

toolsFull.name: swan_verify_matrix
toolsFull.description: The emulator→device parity gate. Only an active device_verified row with exact structured deviceFeature, explicit deviceOutcome:'pass', matching cClass, intact bytes, live-probed non-emulator PICO identity, and same-serial screencap binding closes a feature. Free-text claim polarity is never inferred. Retraction, failed outcome, capture/hash failure, missing lineage, or omitted-subset cache refresh reopens it. No Swan hardware values have been measured in this repo.

app.description: Canonical app/package parity key: lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen; no paths or spaces.

features.description: Headset features to re-test (default: derived from the trust ledger's built_for_headset rows, else all).

deviceSerial.description: Explicit online adb serial. Required when more than one PICO-shaped candidate is attached; unrecognized identities fail closed.

toolsFull.name: run_factory
toolsFull.description: The v6.0 autonomous spatial factory: take a QUEUE of briefs (each with a draft AppSpec) and run the whole pipeline headlessly per brief — PLAN (validate + feasibility lint) → COMPILE (build ledger) → fold in the trust ledger (vision-verified nodes) + parity ledger (built-for-Swan) — then emit a per-brief factory record + a reproducible FLEET DASHBOARD, run the eval scorecard as CI, and reflect (recurring lint warnings across the fleet → candidate record_lesson entries). Deterministic + headless; the per-brief emulator build + vision pass and the Swan flip are driven by the autonomous_spatial_build_v6 prompt. NO aggregate over-claim — a fleet metric never upgrades any node's evidence class; vision_verified counts come only from the trust ledger.

toolsFull.name: capture_canonical
toolsFull.description: DETERMINISTIC capture (v6.2). Grabs the emulator's forward immersive frame via `adb exec-out screencap` — byte-stable across repeated captures and across kill+relaunch (measured MAE=0) because content is authored in the forward FOV and this path does not drift (unlike the GUI free-cam orbit). With recenter:true it sends the actual gRPC xr_command RECENTER first; command acceptance is reported, while its rendered-pose effect remains unverified on emulator 0.13.1. Returns the saved path + content sha256 + dimensions + objective measurements. The bytes are structurally inspected (signature, chunk CRCs, raster) before anything is written: a truncated or non-image screencap is refused rather than saved as the canonical frame. Pass expectSha to detect drift instead of silently verifying a different view.

serial.description: adb device serial (default emulator-5554).

outPath.description: Full-res PNG output path. Default: a run-unique RETAINED file under the observation root, never a fixed shared path a later capture can overwrite. The default TARGET is unchanged (emulator-5554).

recenter.description: Send gRPC xr_command RECENTER before capture. The command is real; its rendered-pose effect is unverified on emulator 0.13.1. Default false.

expectSha.description: Expected content sha256 — the tool reports match/DRIFT instead of silently returning a different view.

toolsFull.name: visual_judge
toolsFull.description: THE CALIBRATED AUTOMATED EYE (v6.3, MR-aware). MEASURES objective properties of a real captured frame (foreground object COUNT via connected-components, dominant colors, non-black coverage, brightness) against an acceptance predicate, and returns a verdict + confidence. This scales verification WITHOUT lying: a judge verdict is EVIDENCE, never human sight. A confident PASS can be recorded (record=true) under the DISTINCT `auto_judged` evidence class — bucketed separately from vision_verified in every report and NEVER upgraded to it. A hard failed check returns FAIL; low confidence returns ESCALATE for a human LOOK. Neither records evidence. It closes the 'N cards render' over-claim by actually counting the objects. Calibrated against the human-verified golden (6 cards → measures 6). MR RULE: on a passthrough/home-env frame (coverage > 0.5 — every Mixed stageStyle '1' capture) the count/black checks are structurally blind and go ADVISORY (they can never auto-PASS); pass expect.authoredColors (the spec's body.color palette) to count objects by color-key detection instead — the real MR auto_judged lane. Without a scorable palette, passthrough frames ALWAYS escalate, by design.

imagePath.description: Path to the captured frame (from capture_canonical / capture_frame).

claim.description: Caller-authored context for why this predicate is being run. It is returned and stored as explicitly unverified context; only the producer-derived expect/check result becomes the measured ledger claim.

maxObjects.description: Maximum foreground objects expected (default minObjects + 1 slack).

notMostlyBlack.description: The frame must not be an empty/black void. Tautological (advisory, zero confidence) on passthrough frames.

colorsPresent.description: Hex colors expected among the dominant colors, e.g. ['#48A552']. Advisory on passthrough frames (the environment dominates the histogram).

authoredColors.description: MR MODE: the spec's AUTHORED object colors. Objects are counted by color-key detection against this palette (the metric layer's saturation-gated detector) — the only check that can score on a passthrough frame. Needs >= 2 distinct (non-neutral) colors to auto-judge; all-neutral palettes degrade honestly to ESCALATE.

expect.description: The acceptance predicate to measure against.

app.description: If set with record=true, records a passing verdict to this app's trust ledger as auto_judged.

record.description: Record a confident PASS to the ledger as auto_judged (default false). Never records vision_verified.

minConfidence.description: Confidence needed for a PASS (default 0.8); below the band → ESCALATE.

toolsFull.name: generate_app_wiring
toolsFull.description: Generate the app-DEFINING wiring from an AppSpec — the files that turn the primitives into a running app, which previously had NO generator and were hand-authored (the ledger→running-app gap). Emits three deterministic Kotlin files: SceneComposition.kt (the build(root) body: load data → SceneRouter for multi-scene or SceneLayout.place + SceneInteraction.register + showDetail for single scene), HomeStage.kt (the SpatialView.initial wiring on the main thread + AgentBridge + DEBUG_CMD dispatch, with branches only for the primitives the spec uses; the menu select/hover whitelist is derived from the spec's actual buttons — custom actions like 'putt' are broadcast-drivable; specs with panels get 'panel:show'/'panel:hide' routing that starts/finishes the panel activity from the app's own context), and Main.kt (the mainApp entrypoint). Analytical/deterministic (same spec → byte-identical wiring). Write each to its path, then build_and_run. Pairs with compile_app_spec (which now lists these as steps). RETURNS: JSON {files: [{path, content}]} — write ALL of them (path is project-relative).

toolsFull.name: generate_panel_compose_kotlin
toolsFull.description: Emit HudPanel.kt — a LIVE-RUNTIME-TEXT spatial panel (the hybrid-app tier). ARCHITECTURE (the proven path): the panel is its OWN 2D ACTIVITY (HudPanelActivity, same APK + process) — the OS auto-hosts every 2D task as a floating spatial panel over the still-rendering immersive scene (vision-verified with Settings, v9.3). An immersive app's own WindowContainer opens on the emulator ONLY when the app explicitly calls spatialNavigator.openWindowContainer(id, tag) — MEASURED 2026-08-06, vision_verified (ledger com.picoagent.v35expb#0), which NARROWS our v9.3 note: that measurement was of a declared-but-never-opened container. Declaring registers it; opening it is a separate call. generate_container_app_kotlin emits that call. This activity lane remains the right answer when you want the shell to own the panel's lifetime independently of any container. Compose state is shared in-process, so DEBUG_CMD 'hud:<key>=<value>' -> HudState.set updates the text LIVE; HudState.onLaunch()/onReset() are game hooks the wiring calls from menu actions (bump 'throws', READY/ROLLING 'status'). Show/hide headlessly: DEBUG_CMD 'panel:show'/'panel:hide' (wired by generate_app_wiring for any spec with panels — show starts the activity from the APP'S OWN context because shell am start is refused while the Stage holds Full Space; hide finishes it via the activity's instance companion, the rocketsim-proven way to un-occlude scene captures). adb shell am start -n <pkg>/<contentPkg>.HudPanelActivity also works when the shell start is not refused. SPATIALUI (v35.1): the hud panel is mounted inside PicoTheme { } and every colour/text size comes from a PicoTheme.colorScheme / PicoTheme.typography ROLE (fillSecondary surface, fillPrimary title, labelSecondary/labelPrimary rows, displayMedium/headlineLarge) — no hardcoded hex, no androidx.compose.material, matching PICO's own samples (0 material imports, 17 PicoTheme wraps). Because PICO's default scheme is light-on-glass, the panel now reads as native glass rather than the previous dark-navy slab. RETURNS: JSON {kotlin, manifestEntry, note} — write kotlin to the targetPath and merge manifestEntry into <application>: the activity with its own taskAffinity so it doesn't replace the immersive task. placement:'world' is accepted and still emits the dock path: no public API world-poses an OS-composited 2D window, which remains true. CORRECTED v35.2 — that limit was over-generalised into 'in-scene 2D is impossible', which is false; generate_attachment_panel_kotlin places Compose INSIDE the 3D scene via AttachmentPanel + TransformComponent (metres), and 'world' now points there in the emitted code + note. Scene placement is still not world-locking; anchors remain deferred.

But our older wording implied in-scene 2D content was impossible, and that was wrong: use generate_attachment_panel_kotlin, where AttachmentPanel inside a SpatialView gives a Compose surface on a real ECS Entity you position in metres (0.13.3, SpatialView.kt:182; six of eight PICO samples use it).
