toolsFull.description: Cross-builder EXTERNAL-APK OBSERVATION: install an arbitrary PICO APK on an EXPLICITLY NAMED serial, launch it, and observe identity — local APK sha256, the installed package and its on-device digest, boot id, PID and process start, foreground package, a bounded PID-scoped logcat, and one inspected screencap published immutably into a unique run directory. Results are STRUCTURAL: an observation, never a run receipt, a release claim or a hardware claim, and nothing is recorded for you. It never clears the global log and never stops an app it was not given: a foreign foreground comes back as a conflict with the evidence. capture route 'adb-screencap': `adb exec-out screencap -p` composites the CURRENT DISPLAY through the device shell. It observes what the display server presents, not what an XR runtime submits to the headset, so an immersive layer can read black here while drawing correctly — and can also read black when nothing is drawn. Treat black as inconclusive about the route and capture a second way.

apkPath.description: Absolute path to the .apk the external builder emitted; its bytes are hashed locally.

serial.description: REQUIRED adb serial of the target device. There is no default: an observation names the device it observed.

activity.description: Fully-qualified launch activity. If omitted, launched via a monkey LAUNCHER intent.

expectLogcatContains.description: Optional substring to look for in the bounded log. Sets logcatMatch true/false; null when not provided.

settleSec.description: Seconds to wait after launch before observing (default 8).

toolsFull.name: generate_set_dressing
toolsFull.description: Emit SetDressing.kt — PROCEDURAL themed SET DRESSING that kills the black void (the #1 AAA gap), v6 = the GEOMETRIC-DENSITY tier: glossy PBR floor, perimeter neon trim, backdrop wall + pinstripes + arcade dot band, lane chevrons + side dashes, corner pillars with glowing caps + torus halo rings + orbs, CEILING BEAMS with hanging neon tube fixtures (fills the top of frame), 45° corner braces, side rails with glowing end caps + posts, a framed marquee with studs, diagonal floor inlays, and a themed light rig (dim IBL + shadowed key + colored points) — ~55 props, all from verified SDK primitives (box/sphere/cylinder/torus), no assets to bake. Themes: neon/showroom/cosmic/noir. Call SetDressing.install(sceneRoot) INSTEAD of a bright SceneLighting.apply. Animate: entities/materials expose 'marquee', 'capNE..SW', 'ringNE..SW' for SceneTimeline.bind. Visual quality still requires a looked-at capture (iterate with fidelity_score; profile dark-theme for neon/noir/cosmic). RETURNS JSON {kotlin, callSnippet, animatables, note}.

withMarquee.description: Include the framed marquee sign bar (default true).

withCeiling.description: Include ceiling beams + hanging fixtures (default true — fills the top of frame).

density.description: Visual-richness vs draw-call budget. 'rich' (~90 props: + side dashes, inlays, orbs, braces, rails, 4th ceiling beam, 9-dot band) is the full AAA dressing for on-device/hardware; 'standard' (~52, DEFAULT) trims to the highest-impact set; 'lite' (~30) for perf-constrained targets. NOTE: a startup FocusEvent ANR observed on the emulator was proven ENVIRONMENTAL (bisect: the bare app with NO dressing ANRs identically) — a degraded emulator focus subsystem after a long session, NOT caused by density; remedy is a cold emulator restart (see diagnose emu_focus_wedge). install() is SUSPEND (yields the main thread during the build) regardless, which is correct for large builds on real hardware.

toolsFull.name: generate_signage_texture
toolsFull.description: Generate an emissive NEON SIGNAGE texture PNG with ImageMagick — the TEXTURE lever for fidelity edgeDetail (flat-shaded geometry can't move it; surface detail can) AND real TEXT (the native SDK has no runtime TextComponent). Styles: 'marquee' (a framed glowing TITLE + tagline), 'grid' (a neon lattice/circuit pattern for fine detail), 'scoreboard' (LANE/FRAME/SCORE rows). Writes a transparent-background PNG at outPath. VERIFY NOW by LOOKING at the PNG (host-side, no emulator). To put it in-world: bake_textured_model(modelPath=<a plane GLB textured with this PNG>, outBundle=assets/sign.bundle) then load it on the backdrop (raw GLB renders black — bake first). Returns {file, width, height, style, next}.

title.description: marquee: the big glowing word (e.g. 'STRIKE!'). scoreboard: the header.

tagline.description: marquee: small line under the title.

accent2.description: Second neon hex for the glow/grid (default #22e0ff cyan).

width.description: Texture width px (default 1024; use POT for GPU).

toolsFull.name: bake_signage_board
toolsFull.description: Bake a signage PNG into an in-world EMISSIVE textured plane (the combined geometry+texture lever). Takes a generate_signage_texture PNG, builds an emissive plane GLB at the image aspect (headless Blender), bakes it to a spatialbundle (the only textured path — raw GLB renders black), and emits SignageBoard<id>.kt that loads + places it at a world position/width on the backdrop. Real crisp TEXT + fine detail in-world (edgeDetail the native SDK can't draw at runtime). RETURNS JSON {bundle, modelName, kotlin, callSnippet, assetName}. Needs ImageMagick output + Blender + the spatialbundle toolchain. Copy the bundle into app/src/main/assets/ and call SignageBoard<id>.load(sceneRoot) in SpatialView.initial.

id.description: Unique id for the emitted loader class + entity name, e.g. 'Marquee' or 'Scoreboard'.

packageName.description: Kotlin package for the loader, e.g. com.demo.bowldeck.content

worldWidth.description: Board width in meters (default 2.6; height derived from PNG aspect).

emissiveStrength.description: Emission multiplier for the neon glow (default 1.4).

toolsFull.name: analyze_splat
toolsFull.description: 3D BOUNDING BOXES ON A GAUSSIAN SPLAT, host-side, in seconds (reproduces PICO's announced OS-6 emulator capability on the CURRENT 0.13 toolchain). Parses .spz (Niantic v2/v3) or binary .ply positions, trims floater outliers (1-99 percentile), voxel-density clusters into top-K axis-aligned boxes, estimates the floor plane, and renders a top-down density HEATMAP with the boxes drawn on it (LOOK at it to verify the boxes wrap real structures — honest host-side verification). Feed the result to generate_splat_colliders to make the splat INTERACTIVE (splats have no native collision). Returns {numPoints, sampled, elapsedMs, global, floorY, clusters, heatmap}.

splatPath.description: Path to the .spz or .ply gaussian splat.

cellSize.description: Voxel size in splat units/meters (default 0.15 — furniture scale).

heatmapOut.description: Heatmap PNG path (default alongside the splat under /tmp/pico-render/splat).

toolsFull.name: generate_splat_colliders
toolsFull.description: Turn analyze_splat's bounding boxes into the INTERACTIVE collider rig (SplatColliders.kt): a static CollisionComponent box per cluster + a floor slab at floorY. Splats expose no native collision mesh, so these measured boxes provide a predictable cheap query proxy. PICO mesh/convex colliders are queryable when real mesh data is available, but their local-space alignment and scale must be handled explicitly. With this rig, Scene.rayCast can hit the splat's clustered structures. Optional debugVisuals renders each box so the fit can be LOOKED at. RETURNS JSON {kotlin, callSnippet}.

floorY.description: Floor height from analyze_splat (adds a floor slab collider; omit to skip).

roomBounds.description: analyze_splat's global bounds — emits 4 WALL slab colliders at the room perimeter (pass OBJECT-kind clusters here, walls come from these bounds; 'structure'-kind boxes usually should NOT be passed as solid boxes — they'd block rayCast through the whole interior).

yUp.description: Splat frame is already Y-up (default true; World Labs Marble splats usually need the same rotation as the splat entity — apply the SAME transform to this rig's parent).

debugVisuals.description: Render each collider as a translucent box mesh (verify the fit in-app; default false).

toolsFull.name: semantic_splat_scan
toolsFull.description: The SEMANTIC layer for a Gaussian splat (visual→geometric→SEMANTIC). Runs analyze_splat for the GEOMETRIC 3D boxes, then renders headless COLOR perspective views covering the room (numpy point projection, no GL — clean + recognizable, unlike the emulator's garbled splat) with each cluster's box drawn + numbered. LOOK at every returned view and label each #id ('counter','neon menu','bottle shelf','floor','stool'…), then call compose_semantic_scene with those labels. This is what lets an agent reference objects by NAME -> auto-framing + auto-placement. HEADLESS MODE: autoLabel=true runs OWL-v2 zero-shot detection over clean renders and returns autoLabels per cluster id — these are auto_judged detector opinions, NOT vision-verified; spot-check the annotated views before trusting a hero label. Returns {clusters, views:[{out,name,visibleIds}], bounds, floorY, autoLabels?}.

splatPath.description: Absolute path to the .ply (or .spz) Gaussian splat.

outDir.description: Where to write the view PNGs (default /tmp/pico-render/semantic/<stem>).

autoLabel.description: Run OWL-v2 zero-shot labeling headlessly over the views (needs transformers+torch in the resolved python; ~1GB model download on first use).

labelQueries.description: Candidate labels for the zero-shot detector (default: a generic indoor vocabulary). Pass scene-specific terms ('ramen bar counter', 'neon menu') for better matches.

toolsFull.name: compose_semantic_scene
toolsFull.description: Turn semantic_splat_scan labels into a STRUCTURED scene: a labeled-object JSON, a RELATIONSHIP graph (on-top-of / next-to / inside, derived from the 3D boxes — so an agent resolves 'the table on the carpet' to the right object), an AUTO-FRAME camera pose that faces a chosen hero label (the fix for the manual pose-sweeping), and AUTO-PLACEMENT of physics on the labeled floor. Pass the clusters back with a label per id. Returns {objects, relationships, autoFrame, placement}. Feed autoFrame into the environment transform and placement into generate_splat_colliders / your physics props.

label.description: What it is, e.g. 'neon menu wall', 'counter', 'bottle shelf', 'stool', 'floor'.

objects.description: The labeled clusters (drop the ones you couldn't identify).

heroLabel.description: Which labeled object to auto-frame the camera on (e.g. 'neon menu wall'). Default: the object with the largest wall-like face.

eyeHeight.description: Standing eye height above the floor for the auto-frame (default 1.3).

toolsFull.name: generate_command_center
toolsFull.description: Scaffold an AGENTIC COMMAND CENTER — a real WebSpatial (React + @webspatial/react-sdk) app where a chat panel talks to an agent and a DISPATCHER opens the right OS-6 window/volume per returned resource type: .glb/.gltf → a 3D VOLUME (model-viewer), video → a window, image → a window, any url → a web panel. This is the PICO 'agentic command center' pattern (workshop OpenClaw kit) on our WebSpatial multi-scene lane (initScene + window.open, correct xr_spatial_scene manifest). Ships a MOCK agent (keyword→resource, so it demos with no backend); set agentEndpoint to a real agent (returns {reply, resources:[{type,url,title}]}) to go live. Build + serve, then `adb reverse tcp:5173`, open in the emulator browser, 'open as app'. Returns {projectDir, files, run}.

projectDir.description: Absolute path to scaffold the app into.

agentEndpoint.description: POST endpoint that takes {message} and returns {reply, resources:[{type:'model'|'video'|'image'|'web', url, title}]}. Omit to use the built-in MOCK agent (keyword→resource).

toolsFull.name: check_toolchain_updates
toolsFull.description: Check whether your installed PICO toolchain is current. Polls the update channel the PICO Android Studio plugin reads plus public Maven metadata, then diffs both against your local install. Reports the advertised versions per (osVersion, package), which artifacts are publicly downloadable, and the installed-vs-available delta — so you can take an upgrade as soon as one is available to you. 'installed' is the emulator and editor of the SELECTED toolchain ($PICO_HOME / spatial.tools.dir / the newest usable version), never a hardcoded location. Each component is selected on its own, so `installed.selection.emulator` and `installed.selection.editor` each disclose the installation THAT version was read from (or the structured unavailable/* reason none could be) — on a host that upgraded one payload and not the other they legitimately differ. Read-only: fetches metadata, downloads nothing.

includeRaw.description: Include the raw channel package list (default false).

toolsFull.name: preflight_env
toolsFull.description: v27-pre READ-ONLY environment doctor: node, adb, emulator/AVD state, gRPC reachability, pico-cli presence (warn-tier — the perf/trace/recording lane is optional), macOS Accessibility (the silent CGEvent-drop gotcha), camera-calibration freshness (dies on emulator cold restart), and disk headroom. Every non-pass check carries the EXACT fix. Run this FIRST on a new machine. Never mutates anything.

status.description: problems = at least one check FAILING (warn/unknown do not fail the doctor).

fix.description: The EXACT next command/action for a non-pass check; null when passing.

toolsFull.name: generate_webspatial_multiview
toolsFull.description: Generate a MULTI-VIEW WebSpatial app (#1, PICO OS 6 'multi-view architecture') — a real, buildable React + @webspatial/react-sdk project with SEVERAL spatial scenes (each an OS-managed window or volume on OS 6). Uses the CORRECT manifest key `xr_spatial_scene` (+ window_scene/volume_scene overrides), registers each secondary scene at runtime via initScene(name, cb, {type}) with its SpatialSceneCreationOptions (defaultSize incl. '0.8m' meter strings for volumes, resizability, worldScaling/worldAlignment/baseplateVisibility), opens scenes with window.open(url, name), and renders per-scene routes with enable-xr panels + a 2D-projection preview.html. Verify with verify_webspatial_scenes (static scene-graph + headless boot). Spatial behavior = built_for_os6; the 2D projection is verifiable today.

projectDir.description: Directory to write the project into.

name.description: Scene id (route + window.open target + initScene name), e.g. 'detail'.

toolsFull.name: verify_webspatial_scenes
toolsFull.description: Verify a WebSpatial app's MULTI-VIEW scene graph (#2, headless — no device). STATIC: reads the manifest's xr_spatial_scene (+ overrides) and scans the source for initScene(name,...,{type}), window.open(url,name) scene-opens, and enable-xr elements → the declared scene graph (deterministic). RUNTIME (optional, pass servedUrl of the BUILT+served app): drives headless Chrome with a PicoWebApp UA and confirms it BOOTS as a picoos WebSpatial app (React mounts, no JS exceptions, content renders) + screenshots the 2D projection. HONEST: the scene graph is structural; the 2D render is vision-verifiable; NATIVE spatial-scene command emission needs the real PICO OS 6 runtime (built_for_os6 — a stubbed bridge runs the SDK in polyfill/degraded mode, confirmed). Returns {sceneGraph, boot, screenshot}.

projectDir.description: The WebSpatial project dir (or its built dir) — for the static scene-graph scan.

servedUrl.description: URL of the BUILT + served app (e.g. http://localhost:PORT/index.html) for the headless boot/render check. Omit for static-only.

toolsFull.name: ingest_marble_world
toolsFull.description: Ingest a downloaded World-Labs / Marble world (.spz splat or .glb mesh) into an INTERACTIVE native emulator scene — one call. For .spz: analyze_splat (3D bounding boxes + floor) -> generate_splat_colliders (the collider rig so objects rest on / rayCast hits the world's furniture — splats have NO native collision) -> generate_environment_kotlin kind='splat' (the SplatEnvironment loader) -> the exact HomeStage wiring + the adb-push. For .glb: the bake_textured_model path (a SOLID, view-INDEPENDENT render). Writes the Kotlin into projectDir/content if given, and returns {files, adbPush, homeStageSnippet, analysis, notes}. Then build_and_run + capture. HONEST: a splat renders as a photoreal but VIEW-DEPENDENT bounded volumetric window (the C4 SpatialView ceiling) — apply the fillMaxSize + world-scale fix (in the notes) so it FILLS the view; a .glb mesh is the reliable-render alternative (Blender can texture it).

worldPath.description: Absolute path to the downloaded .spz or .glb.

projectDir.description: If given, writes the generated Kotlin into <projectDir>/app/src/main/java/<pkg>/content/ and (.spz) prints the adb-push into the app's external files dir.

withColliders.description: .spz only: auto-extract + emit the interactive collider rig (default true).

scale.description: World scale (splats/meshes often want ~1.0-2.2 to fill a walkable space; default 1).

toolsFull.name: fidelity_score
toolsFull.description: AAA-quality RUBRIC over a capture PNG — host-side ImageMagick heuristics only (no adb). Returns five 0-100 subscores (nonVoid = lit fraction, contrast = luminance spread, colorVariety = mean saturation, edgeDetail = edge density, brightBalance = exposure vs the 0.18-0.55 mid band), a weighted total (30/20/20/20/10), a grade (>=80 AAA, >=60 solid, >=40 flat, else void), and a concrete tool-named fix suggestion for every subscore below 55 — the quality bar that tells an agent WHAT to fix next. HONESTY: this is a heuristic auto_judged-class signal for ITERATION — it is NOT a substitute for LOOKING at the frame; record_verification still requires a looked-at capture, and a high score must never be claimed as vision_verified.

imagePath.description: Path to the capture PNG (from capture_canonical / capture_frame).

label.description: Optional label for this scoring run, e.g. 'knockdown forward view after lighting pass'.

profile.description: Weighting profile. 'dark-theme' (neon/noir/cosmic art direction) reweights to nonVoid 10 / contrast 25 / colorVariety 30 / edgeDetail 25 / brightBalance 10 and widens the exposure band down to 0.06 — an intentionally dark scene is NOT a void; judge it on color/contrast/detail instead.

region.description: 'full' (default) scores the whole frame. 'content' auto-trims near-black margins first (magick -fuzz -trim) and scores only the lit CONTENT bounding box — the honest measure for a dark scene where content sits in a band with black margins (the free-cam can't dolly closer, so the void around good content would otherwise cap the score). Reports the trimmed fraction.

toolsFull.name: capture_rig
toolsFull.description: Deterministic multi-angle capture rig for the DRIFTING emulator free-cam (ceiling C2). Recovers pitch (drags hard down then recoverDy back), then sweeps sweepSteps fixed yaw increments of stepDx px, screencapping at each stop, and scores every frame (nonVoid 0.5 + saturation 0.3 + edges 0.2 via magick; falls back to file size if magick is missing). Returns ALL scored frames + the top-<keep> paths. HONESTY: scores are auto_judged-class heuristics AT BEST — this tool only RANKS; it is NOT a substitute for LOOKING. The CALLER must still LOOK at the best frames (e.g. Read them) before claiming anything vision_verified. macOS-only (drives the qemu GUI cam; needs Accessibility). Pairs with emulator_look (single aimed look) and capture_frame.

recoverDy.description: Recovery pitch drag after the hard-down: default 400 (down) to counter upward drift; pass negative to pitch up.

sweepSteps.description: Yaw stops in the sweep (default 10, max 24).

stepDx.description: Horizontal drag px per stop (default 180; negative sweeps left).

keep.description: How many best paths to return (default 3).

settleMs.description: Wait after each drag before screencap (default 400).

normalize.description: Run the hard pitch-recovery before sweeping (default true). Set FALSE to sweep gently around the CURRENT pose — e.g. right after an app launch, whose default forward pose often already frames the content (verified: the fresh-launch pose framed the neon alley; the hard recovery lost it).

toolsFull.name: measure_perf
toolsFull.description: Performance/smoothness probe for AAA claims: reset + sample `dumpsys gfxinfo <pkg>` frame stats (total/janky frames, 50/90/95/99th percentile frame times) and `dumpsys meminfo` PSS on the emulator, then verdict: p90<=16.7ms & janky<10% -> smooth (60fps-class), p90<=33.4ms -> acceptable (30fps-class), else janky; no stats -> no-frame-data. Missing fields are null, never fabricated. HONESTY: gfxinfo covers the app's UI/RenderThread frames (Compose panels, WebViews, 2D activities). The immersive Filament/OpenXR scene path may NOT be measured by gfxinfo on this emulator — if frame data is absent or tiny while the app runs, that means exactly that: only the measured UI surfaces are reported; do not extrapolate this verdict to the 3D scene. Evidence class: structural — not a substitute for LOOKING at a capture.

packageName.description: App package to probe, e.g. com.example.showroomxr

resetFirst.description: Reset gfxinfo stats before sampling (default true) so numbers cover only the sample window.

sampleSec.description: Seconds to sample before reading stats (default 10, max 60).

toolsFull.name: generate_animation_timeline
toolsFull.description: Emit SceneTimeline.kt — a MULTI-TRACK keyframe choreography driver. EXTENDS the vision-verified SceneAnimator runtime-motion path (generate_scene_animator_kotlin): identical per-frame `entity.components.set(TransformComponent(pos, rot.toQuat(), scale))` on the main thread + the same coroutine frame-loop. Each track carries position/rotation(deg)/scale/emissive keyframes; the driver LINEARLY interpolates between them over a shared timeline (loop or hold). Bind runtime entities by name: SceneTimeline.bind("planet", planetEntity, planetMat); then LaunchedEffect(Unit){ SceneTimeline.run() }. HONEST SCOPE: transform + emissive keyframe choreography only — NOT skeletal/rigged/morph animation (unsupported). Emissive is grayscale intensity (Color4(v,v,v,1f)); needs a PhysicallyBasedMaterial bound. Expected evidence class once driven + captured: vision_verified via before/after motion frames (this tool extends the vision-verified SceneAnimator path but is not itself LOOKED-at until you capture it). RETURNS JSON {kotlin, note} — write to content/SceneTimeline.kt.

target.description: Track name — you bind the runtime Entity to it via SceneTimeline.bind(name, entity).

emissiveColor.description: RGB 0..1 tint for the emissive channel: keyframe e drives setEmissiveColor(Color4(r*e,g*e,b*e,1)) — keeps neon COLORED while pulsing (default [1,1,1] = white/grayscale)

emissive.description: Emissive intensity 0..1 (needs a PBR material bound).

keyframes.description: Keyframes; any channel may be omitted per key (each channel interpolates over the keys that set it).

tracks.description: The animation tracks (several objects moving in concert).

loop.description: Loop the timeline forever (default true); false = play once and hold the last keyframe.

durationSec.description: Timeline length in seconds (default = the max keyframe time across all tracks).

toolsFull.name: generate_spatial_audio
toolsFull.description: FALLBACK LANE (see the retraction in this file's header): SDK 0.13.3 DOES ship a runtime spatial-audio API (AudioResource + entity.prepareAudio + AudioPlayerController, verified in core-0.13.3-sources.jar and used by PICO's own SpatialAudio sample) — an earlier note here wrongly said it did not. This tool deliberately emits Android SoundPool instead: a positional TRIGGER with crude distance/pan, no SDK dependency, no HRTF. Prefer the SDK path for new work. Emit SpatialAudioSource.kt — add a POSITIONED audio source to a scene at a world position, started when the app runs. HONEST SCOPE: a grep of the installed SDK 0.13.3 found NO runtime spatial-audio Kotlin API (only the editor's USD SpatialAudioFile authoring schema), so this does NOT use SDK HRTF — it FALLS BACK to Android SoundPool, loading the bundled asset and playing it at app start with a CRUDE distance-attenuation + L/R pan from the position (a positional TRIGGER, not spatialization). EVIDENCE: structural — compiles + app runs + logcat shows audio init/stream id (tag SpatialAudioSource); audio is NOT visually verifiable and TRUE HRTF spatialization is built_for_headset (PICO Swan). Call SpatialAudioSource.start(context) from your scene onCreate/onResume and stop() on teardown; put <assetName> in src/main/assets/. RETURNS JSON {kotlin, manifestEntry, note, evidence}. For entity-attached SDK audio see generate_spatial_audio_kotlin.

assetName.description: Audio file bundled under src/main/assets/, e.g. 'ambient.ogg' (SoundPool: short clips; .ogg/.wav).

position.description: World position [x,y,z] in meters the sound is conceptually anchored at; used for a crude distance/pan hint (NOT true HRTF).

loop.description: Loop forever (SoundPool loop=-1) vs play once (default false).

toolsFull.name: virtual_camera_frame
toolsFull.description: Render a deterministic host-side synthetic camera frame from a scanned world model. The pose is in app coordinates; pass an occupancy-grid JSON as worldConfig to apply its exact offsetApplied mapping back to raw-splat coordinates. calibratedIntrinsics uses ~/.pico-mcp/camera-calibration.json (f/cx/cy). This is explicitly NOT an emulator camera capture.

toolsFull.name: virtual_camera_surfaces
toolsFull.description: Simulate camera-visible support-plane detection from a semantic scanned-room model. Reports detector-labeled floor/object tops, whole-surface visibleFraction plus detectedPatchVisibleFraction/visiblePatchFraction, center-ray occupancy LOS, distance, and extents for an arbitrary pose. A tiny visible sliver cannot pass a high minVisibleFraction. Structural geometry only; losClear is null without occupancyPath.

toolsFull.name: virtual_camera_from_app
toolsFull.description: Capture the foreground PICO emulator app, render the scanned world from the same explicitly reported pose, simulate visible surfaces, and compose a labeled side-by-side. The default pose is an assumption: the bridge has scene entities but NO live head pose. The adb image is a real emulator display capture; the companion frame is host synthetic (usd_host_render at best), and the composition earns no visual claim until LOOKed at.

toolsFull.name: generate_procedural_asset
toolsFull.description: Generate a DETERMINISTIC parametric 3D prop as a USDA mesh (shape + PBR color) — the offline, no-network, byte-reproducible content source for generative depth. spatialbundle bakes the USDA into a renderable bundle with a UsdPreviewSurface material (VERIFIED). Shapes: cube/gem/octahedron/tetrahedron/pyramid/prism/crystal + LATHE solids pin/bottle (revolved real silhouettes — for knockdown/bowling props keep the capsule COLLIDER and use the lathe mesh as the MODEL). Flat-shaded crisp facets, planar UVs. Analytical (same params → identical USDA, so the determinism/regression gates hold). Returns the USDA text + a suggested outBundle name; WRITE it to a .usda, then bake_textured_model it, then bind via object.source="model" (import_model_catalog does a batch). Use this instead of a hosted API when you want deterministic, free, distinct per-item props.

shape.description: The parametric prop shape. pin/bottle are LATHE solids (a revolved silhouette — a real bowling-pin/bottle shape, not a capsule); size = their full HEIGHT.

name.description: Asset name (the model name inside the bundle + the .usda/.bundle stem), e.g. 'ruby'.

toolsFull.name: structural_asset_gate
toolsFull.description: HONESTY TIER 1 of 3 for generative depth: validate a 3D asset (.glb/.gltf/.usda/.usd) STRUCTURALLY before it enters the pipeline — real geometry, a triangle budget (perf), a finite/sane bounding box, UVs (if it should be textured), a material present, and NOT Draco-compressed (Assimp can't load Draco → empty bundle). Returns metrics (triangles, bbox size, hasUVs/Material/textures, sha256) + a pass/fail with concrete failures. Optionally records `structural` to the app's trust ledger (never vision_verified — a structural pass proves WELL-FORMED + IN-BUDGET, never that it looks good). This is the gate a generated/imported asset must clear before bake → bind → render → auto_judged → human vision_verified.

requireUVs.description: Fail if no UVs (default false — set true for textured assets).

app.description: If set, records a `structural` ledger entry for this app on pass.

claim.description: The claim to record (defaults to a generic asset-validated claim).

toolsFull.name: text_to_3d
toolsFull.description: OPT-IN hosted text→3D (Meshy/Tripo/Luma → GLB) for generative depth — the high-fidelity, network-gated half of the hybrid strategy. Because hosted generation is non-deterministic + costs money, it is CACHE-PINNED: a prompt → a deterministic cache key → the GLB is fetched ONCE, hashed, and cached under ~/.pico-mcp/gen-assets/; the same prompt then returns the same sha-pinned GLB (treat it as committed data — the determinism/regression gates stay honest). PROVIDERS: provider='meshy' (or env PICO_TEXT3D_PROVIDER=meshy) uses Meshy's public API with PICO_TEXT3D_KEY and requests origin_at:'bottom' — eliminating the baseLift burial trap by construction (the mrtable table landed origin-CENTRED; measured 2026-07-29) — via the documented preview→refine→model_urls.glb flow; HONESTY: that request shape is per Meshy's docs and has NOT been exercised live from this repo (gated_api — the first keyed call is the verification; still run measure_model on the result and expect baseLift≈0). Otherwise a generic endpoint via env PICO_TEXT3D_ENDPOINT (POST {prompt} → GLB or {url}). With NO provider configured it DEFERS and recommends generate_procedural_asset (deterministic, offline). A hosted asset is still just an asset: it MUST clear structural_asset_gate → bake → bind → render → auto_judged → human vision_verified. Generation NEVER implies quality.

prompt.description: The text description of the model, e.g. 'a low-poly treasure chest'.

provider.description: Force a provider. 'meshy' needs env PICO_TEXT3D_KEY; 'custom' needs PICO_TEXT3D_ENDPOINT. Default: PICO_TEXT3D_PROVIDER / endpoint-configured.

polyBudget.description: Requested detail (default low — respect the tri budget). For meshy: target_polycount 3k/10k/30k.

maxWaitSec.description: meshy only: total budget for the preview+refine task polling.

force.description: Bypass the cache and regenerate (costs a call; default false).

toolsFull.name: import_world_environment
toolsFull.description: Load a CUSTOM photoreal world (World Labs / Marble) as the app's environment — the user stands inside their own scanned/generated world instead of a default home env. Handles the two things that actually break custom-world loading (empirically diagnosed): (1) DELIVERY — ships the splat FROM_STORAGE (adb push) so Android doesn't zip-compress it (which breaks the native loader); (2) CALIBRATION — decodes the file's bbox + DENSITY-weighted centroid + floor, and emits an auto-calibrated transform that places the viewer inside the real geometry (not out in the open air). Accepts a Gaussian splat (.spz / .ply-splat — rendered natively, VERIFIED 1.92M pts) or a MESH (.glb → bake path; .ply-mesh → export GLB from Marble). Returns the inspection, the adb push command, the generate_environment_kotlin call with the calibrated transform, and the capture→LOOK→adjust fine-tune loop. Splats have no collision → also emit a floor box-collider for interaction.

yawDeg.description: Facing yaw about Y (default 180 — faces the interior for Marble; try 0/90/270 in the LOOK loop).

scale.description: Uniform world scale override (default 1 — Marble is metric).

toolsFull.name: render_usd_offscreen
toolsFull.description: Render a USD scene (.usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz — a procedural asset, a composition, etc.) to a PNG OFF-DEVICE on the Mac host via usdrecord + Hydra Storm: deterministic, HD, sub-second, NO emulator, NO build. The requested output is published only after usdrecord exits 0, the fresh output is a validated raster, and the analyzer measures non-black, non-empty content. Returns the PNG path, a content sha256, and objective measurements (object count / colors / coverage). Optionally records a `usd_host_render` ledger entry whose canonical claim contains only those measured facts plus asset/output hashes. This DISTINCT evidence class is NOT the on-device Filament appearance and does not prove caller-authored semantic prose. Use it to PRE-CHECK a generated asset/composition fast, before the expensive bake→build→emulator cycle. (Meshes should be doubleSided or have correct outward normals, or backfaces render dark.)

camera.description: Camera prim path/name in the asset (default: usdrecord auto-frames the geometry).

app.description: If set with record=true, records a `usd_host_render` ledger entry for this app.

claim.description: Caller-authored context for the render request. It is stored as explicitly unverified metadata; it never becomes the measured ledger claim.

toolsFull.name: prepare_ibl_cubemap
toolsFull.description: Author a BRIGHT prefiltered floating-point IBL cubemap (.ktx) so PBR METALS SHINE with studio reflections — wraps Filament's cmgen (equirect → R11F_G11F_B10F cubemap w/ roughness mips, the format ImageBasedLightComponent wants). Provide your own equirect HDR/PNG, OR auto-generate an LDR procedural PNG (preset: studio | sky | neutral). Place the output .ktx under app assets, then wire it with generate_ibl_kotlin(mode='local', intensityExponent≈6) + tag the metallic meshes. VISION-VERIFIED recipe: cmgen studio cubemap → gold/chrome reflected the softbox on the emulator. Requires cmgen at ~/.pico-mcp/bin/cmgen (Filament release binary).

equirect.description: Path to an equirectangular (2:1) HDR/EXR/PNG env image. If omitted, one is auto-generated from `preset`.

preset.description: Auto-generated environment when no equirect is given (default studio).

toolsFull.name: run_immersive_boundary_experiment
toolsFull.description: Run one receipt-bound immersive boundary experiment as staged prepare → reviewed step(s) → exact-hash adjudication → one logical once-only recovery attempt. Recovery executes at most one ordered fallback per call; each continuation supplies reviewedPriorFrame for the preceding fallback's post-frame, so a structural candidate cannot suppress LOOK or unlock a later intervention by itself. Collection never assigns pixel semantics. Full-surface only; explicit serial and an external non-existing artifact root are mandatory.

toolsFull.name: run_in_app_locomotion_route
toolsFull.description: Run one receipt-bound Full-stage in-app world-root route as strict prepare, reviewed step, restore, and structural adjudicate actions. A receipt-bound prior foreground is withheld and not relaunched because relaunch would orphan its immutable receipt. Every mutation uses one explicit direct or replacement mechanism, exact serial and runtime binding, stable captures, safety/continuity evidence, and a caller-reserved external artifact root. Returned captures still require LOOK; the tool does not award visual or device verification.

toolsFull.name: pico_build_app
toolsFull.description: DOOR 1 — Build an evidence-scoped spatial app from a brief. TWO-STEP by design: call with just {brief} to receive a scaffold AppSpec (the planner never guesses your intent — YOU author); adapt the scaffold to the brief, then call again with {brief, draftSpec} to compile through the full pipeline (scaffold → codegen → a fail-closed native run receipt). Apps default to the Mixed stage (stageStyle '1' — the passthrough home environment is the backdrop and content seats ON the room, mrtable-style); a fully-virtual app remains a first-class opt-in via meta.stageStyle '3' (Full). A recorded receipt is structural provenance for one exact build/install/session/capture, not visual proof. Returns its receiptId, receiptPath, and exact immutable capture; LOOK at that capture before claiming how it renders. Even a recorded calibrated-eye PASS returns 'auto-judged-needs-look', never 'verified': only the later human/agent LOOK can earn vision_verified.

brief.description: What to build, e.g. 'a primitive table standing on my real floor with bodies dropping onto it from a clickable menu' (Mixed-stage MR, the default; a fully-virtual brief opts into stage style 3).

draftSpec.description: Your AppSpec, adapted from the scaffold a brief-only call returns. Omit on the first call.

toolsFull.name: pico_scan_world
toolsFull.description: DOOR 2 — Scan a Gaussian-splat world (.ply/.spz, e.g. a World Labs Marble export) into a LABELED semantic scene: geometric clusters + headless renders + OWL-v2 zero-shot labels + a relationship graph. Returns the semantic scene JSON path to feed pico_place / anchorTo briefs, plus the annotated views to spot-check (labels are detector opinions until you LOOK).

labelQueries.description: Scene-specific vocabulary ('bar counter', 'neon sign') — sharper labels than the generic default.

toolsFull.name: pico_place
toolsFull.description: DOOR 3 — Resolve a natural-language anchor against a scanned world: 'in front of the neon sign' → a concrete world position, with fuzzy matching and honest ambiguity/not-found reporting. Feed the result into an AppSpec object transform, or use anchorTo:{label} in a brief for the compiler to do this automatically.

toolsFull.name: pico_look
toolsFull.description: DOOR 4 — Capture the emulator's current display through the device shell and return the image path. Default target emulator-5554 (retained this checkpoint); this door has no serial input. ROUTE: `screencap` composites the display the shell presents, not what an XR runtime submits to the headset — for an immersive layer it can read black while the app renders correctly, and can read black when nothing is drawn, so black is inconclusive about the route rather than a rendering verdict; the bytes are structurally inspected before they are saved. READ the image; that look is what turns a claim into vision_verified (record it with pico_record). NO pose control exists on this path: deterministic = the fixed forward screencap; the multi-angle alternatives are Accessibility-gated GUI drags whose free-cam drifts — so bring content into the forward FOV instead of moving the camera. OCCLUSION: a docked HUD/menu panel can cover the scene; when the app's generated wiring routes the panel DEBUG_CMDs, drive 'panel:hide' before a scene capture and 'panel:show' after (adb shell am broadcast -a <pkg>.DEBUG_CMD --es cmd panel:hide). Apps without that route ignore the broadcast — confirm with the capture itself, never by assumption.

toolsFull.name: pico_verify_app
toolsFull.description: DOOR 5 — OBSERVE any external PICO APK on an EXPLICITLY NAMED device: install → installed-digest check → launch → settle → identity (boot id, PID + process start, foreground) → bounded PID-scoped log → one structurally inspected capture, published immutably into a unique run directory. Works for apps this server never built (including official PICO samples). The result is a STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION, never a run receipt, a release claim or a hardware claim, and no verdict is machine-assigned: it returns identity plus the capture, and YOU look. It never clears the device's global log and never stops an app it was not given — a foreign foreground comes back as a conflict with the evidence.

serial.description: REQUIRED adb serial of the device to observe. There is no default: an observation names the device it observed.

activity.description: Fully-qualified launch activity; omitted means a monkey LAUNCHER intent.

toolsFull.name: pico_measure
toolsFull.description: DOOR 6 — MEASURE a placement in a capture (v20 metric layer): color-keyed detection + calibrated-camera projection → error in px and meters, box IoU. Requires a one-time camera calibration — pico_doctor reports calibration state, and pico_doctor {calibrate:true} performs it end-to-end through the full-surface inner server. Refuses occluded/absent targets instead of guessing.

toolsFull.name: pico_perf
toolsFull.description: DOOR 7 — Profile a running app with PICO's OFFICIAL profiler (pico-cli perf): FPS percentiles, CPU/GPU, jank windows, and PICO's own diagnosis engine. Structural evidence — numbers, not looks. The target is the explicit `device` you pass or the wrapper's documented default; either way the result names it as requestedDevice.

device.description: adb serial to profile; forwarded verbatim. Omitted: the wrapper's documented default target.

toolsFull.name: pico_sdk
toolsFull.description: DOOR 8 — Look up the EXACT PICO Spatial SDK declaration (constructors with parameter order and unit docs, properties, enum values) from the locally materialized agent-vault before writing SDK code — by default the HISTORICAL 0.13.3 declarations, labeled with the package revision their package.xml declares. The app skeleton builds on SDK 6.0.0; docs/SDK_6_0_0_DRIFT.md records the measured near-zero public-API drift as historical evidence, not target authority. Pass projectRoot (optionally vaultRoot / sdkVersion / recordPaths) and the answer reports declarationIdentity, target and declarationContext — target-compatible only when a reviewed compatibility record verifies against the local vault bytes and that project's exact resolved SDK; otherwise unknown/historical, and it says so. Hints select what is read; nothing here accepts an identity, a fingerprint or a compatibility verdict from the caller. All-Float signatures compile silently with swapped args — check first.

projectRoot.description: Android project root hint: its declared BOM/identity are read statically (never Gradle) and reviewed compatibility evidence is verified against it. Omit for a plain historical lookup.

vaultRoot.description: Explicit agent-vault root — an explicitly identified source, not proof of target compatibility.

sdkVersion.description: Numeric vault workspace label under the tools root (e.g. '0.13'); never a path.

recordPaths.description: Reviewed compatibility record paths to consider; only records in the packaged reviewed index can be accepted.

toolsFull.name: pico_doctor
toolsFull.description: DOOR 9 — Health-check the local PICO environment: the read-only preflight (node/adb/emulator/gRPC/Accessibility/calibration/disk — every failure carries the exact fix), toolchain payloads, emulator state, and the v20 camera calibration. Run this FIRST on a new machine, and whenever anything smells off. Pass {calibrate:true} to also RUN the one-time camera calibration end-to-end (fleet_build(['calib']) → calibrate_capture_camera): the inner child server already runs the FULL surface, so no surface switch or client restart is needed — it does need a running emulator and takes a few minutes.

calibrate.description: Build+launch the calib brief and solve the capture camera through the full-surface inner server. Requires a running emulator; takes minutes.

toolsFull.name: pico_ship
toolsFull.description: DOOR 10 — Transparently run the honest ship checklist for an app/lane/project. Native debug provenance clears only when current bytes match a digest-bound v1 run receipt and its exact capture has an effective receipt-linked LOOK. The debug receipt never clears release APK, release signing, store, web-deploy, Swan-hardware, or Windows boundaries.

app.description: Canonical native applicationId or web app ledger key.

projectDir.description: Current project directory whose bytes the checklist must validate (uses ship_checklist's lane default when omitted).

toolsFull.name: pico_capabilities
toolsFull.description: DOOR 11 — What can this toolchain actually do, and how is each capability PROVEN? Generated from the trust ledger: every row's best evidence class, with vision_verified meaning a human/agent looked at a rendered frame.

toolsFull.name: pico_fix
toolsFull.description: DOOR 12 — Paste a build/runtime error (or describe a wrong render) and get the matched retained-lesson: the known root cause and the exact fix, from a corpus of verified past failures. Free text is fine — it is mapped to the diagnosis knowledge base by keyword, and always run through the retained-lessons rulebook. Also lints provided Kotlin against the gotcha rulebook + the official SDK vault. Once you SOLVE a novel gotcha, re-call with {recordLesson:{...}} to persist it as a new lint rule (passed through to record_lesson on the full-surface inner server).

error.description: The error text, logcat excerpt, or symptom description.

kotlin.description: The suspect emitted Kotlin, if available.

pattern.description: A JS regex source string that detects the anti-pattern.

kinds.description: Which content kinds this applies to (default ['any']).

designRule.description: The DESIGN.md rule / diagnose symptom it maps to.

positiveFixture.description: A sample that MUST trigger the rule.

negativeFixture.description: A sample that MUST NOT trigger the rule.

recordLesson.description: After you SOLVE a novel gotcha: persist it as a retained-lessons lint rule. Passed through unchanged to record_lesson, which validates the regex + fixtures before persisting.

toolsFull.name: pico_record
toolsFull.description: DOOR 13 — RECORD a caller-attested verification claim AFTER you LOOKED, append an honest RETRACTION, or explicitly PROMOTE a native receipt into portable one-hop provenance without creating evidence. The three actions are mutually exclusive. Portable record binding requires both runReceiptId and runReceiptPromotionId; native binding omits the promotion ID. Image evidence needs a real PNG/JPEG plus attestation. device_verified additionally requires live hardware/capture binding plus structured deviceFeature and explicit pass/fail outcome.

app.description: Canonical lowercase app/package ledger key: ASCII lowercase letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen; no paths, spaces, or case aliases.

action.description: Default record; retract appends a correction; promote publishes portable one-hop receipt objects without evidence.

claim.description: Record action: the claim, e.g. '6 shelf cards render in the forward FOV'.

evidenceType.description: Record action: a caller-recordable evidence tier. vision_verified needs a linked capture + attestation; device_verified additionally uses live device/capture provenance. auto_judged and usd_host_render are producer-only and must come from visual_judge or render_usd_offscreen.

artifactPath.description: Path to the capture you LOOKED at (REQUIRED for vision_verified).

attestation.description: What you saw in the capture (REQUIRED for vision_verified).

runReceiptId.description: Record action only: receiptId returned by pico_build_app. Pass it after LOOKING at that receipt's exact capture; it binds provenance without promoting the evidence class.

runReceiptPromotionId.description: Record action only: promotionId returned with a portable receipt. Omit it for native receipt binding.

deviceSerial.description: Attached adb serial (REQUIRED for device_verified; probed live).

deviceModel.description: Optional expected model; mismatch with live probe rejects.

deviceFingerprint.description: Optional expected fingerprint; mismatch with live probe rejects.

deviceBootQemu.description: Optional expected ro.boot.qemu; mismatch rejects and live '1' is never hardware.

deviceFeature.description: device_verified only: exact lowercase feature slug measured on-device (for example controller_ray); required with deviceOutcome.

deviceOutcome.description: device_verified only: explicit observed outcome. Swan parity closes only an exact deviceFeature with pass; claim prose is never interpreted.

targetSeq.description: Retract action: sequence number of the claim being corrected.

retractionReason.description: Retract action: why the earlier claim is withdrawn.

retractionNote.description: Retract action: optional nuance retained with the correction.

sourceReceiptId.description: Promote action only: exact native source receipt identity.

sourceReceiptRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical source receipt-store root.

sourceLedgerRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical source ledger-store root.

targetReceiptRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical target receipt-store root.

targetLedgerRoot.description: Promote action only: explicit canonical target ledger-store root.

report.description: Also return ledger_report's generated capability report for the app.

toolsFull.name: pico_emulator
toolsFull.description: DOOR 14 — Emulator lifecycle without leaving the doors surface. {action:'status'} reports adb/boot/gRPC state; {action:'boot'} boots the PICO OS6 emulator headless and waits for Android (fails honestly if one is already online); {action:'restart'} returns the documented COLD-restart command instead of running it — the cold restart kills the qemu process by PID and relaunches with explicit -sysdir/-kernel (adb reboot is insufficient for a wedged ContainerManager), which touches the host process table, so a human runs it.

action.description: status = report state; boot = boot + wait for Android; restart = get the exact cold-restart command (NOT executed).

toolsFull.name: pico_next
toolsFull.description: DOOR 15 — What should I do NOW? Reads the ACTUAL local state — preflight checks, emulator, camera calibration, your generated briefs with their build/capture/trust-ledger progress — and returns {situation, nextAction:{door,argsExample,why}, alternatives}. Every recommendation names a real door on this surface; nothing is executed for you, and a LOOK step still means YOU read the capture.

toolsFull.name: pico_loop
toolsFull.description: DOOR 16 — Declarative build→verify→repair loop (2026-08 Loop Engineering lane): state a goal, acceptance criteria (structural / visual / logcat / perf), and a budget; the loop plans, builds through the fleet pipeline, machine-checks every criterion, and when a failure matches a retained lesson with a concrete AppSpec mutation, applies replan_spec and iterates. Failures without a safe automatic mutation exit manual-repair-required with their measured detail; the loop never relabels them build_failed or pretends an unattended fix occurred. Each iteration opens a marker window (adb_shell `log -t pico-mcp <marker>`) before its build and scopes every logcat criterion to it through assert_logcat's sinceMarker — the device log is never cleared, and a window whose marker is never seen makes that criterion unmeasurable, not failed. Logcat criteria are evaluated before structural asserts (a stable order kept from when assert_scene cleared logcat). HONESTY CEILING BY EVIDENCE: a calibrated-eye PASS earns `auto_judged` only when the matching ledger write succeeds; a measured PASS with a rejected/missing write remains `structural`. An iteration whose requested structural/logcat/perf criteria pass while the eye FAILs, ESCALATEs, or is unscored remains `structural` — it never inherits a visual tier from the word accepted. The loop returns a remainingLookObligation naming the artifacts a person or vision-capable agent must still LOOK at before any vision_verified claim. A no-progress detector stops after two consecutive iterations failing with the identical signature; an unmeasurable criterion (missing perf utilities, no Agent Bridge) stops the loop honestly instead of silently passing; an eye ESCALATE (a frame class the machine cannot judge, e.g. high-coverage passthrough) exits built-needs-look once everything measurable passes — escalation is a look obligation, never a defect to repair. An absent or unknown eye score uses the same terminal status but is labeled unscored, never misreported as an escalation. PERF LOOP LANE: a perf criterion measures with pico-cli and carries its diagnosis into the failure detail. It re-measures only when another applicable retained lesson actually mutates the AppSpec; a generic low-FPS result has no safe automatic quality tradeoff and exits for manual repair. Every measured iteration's pico-cli appFps numbers are ledgered and returned as perfTrend (before→after, structural evidence), and a perf failure carries pico-cli's own diagnosis engine verdict, never a guess. Every iteration writes a structural trust-ledger entry. Each native run also returns a structural receiptId/receiptPath and its exact immutable capture; the receipt proves identity and continuity, never what the pixels look like, so the returned capture still requires a LOOK. Budget uses meta.budget semantics (iterations, timeMin). Builds take minutes each — configure your host's MCP timeout accordingly (≥ 10 minutes, more for multi-iteration budgets). Prefer authoring a draftSpec first (pico_build_app's two-step); goal-only runs start from the planner's archetype scaffold, declared in the result.

goal.description: What to build/achieve, e.g. 'a knockdown game with three stacked crates on my real table'. Used as the brief; also keys the fleet project + ledger.

draftSpec.description: An authored AppSpec to iterate from (recommended — the planner never guesses intent as well as you author it). Omitted: the loop starts from the planner's archetype scaffold and says so.

kind.description: structural = Agent Bridge scene asserts; visual = the calibrated eye's PASS on the canonical capture (auto_judged; ESCALATE becomes built-needs-look, while a missing/unknown result is explicitly unscored); logcat = assert_logcat pattern; perf = pico-cli appFps p5 floor.

entitiesPresent.description: structural: entity names that must exist.

componentsPresent.description: structural: component class names that must exist.

pattern.description: logcat: case-insensitive regex that must appear (REQUIRED for kind:'logcat').

acceptance.description: The exit bar. Every criterion must pass in the SAME iteration for the loop to accept.

timeMin.description: Soft wall-clock budget in minutes (default 20; checked between iterations).

toolCalls.description: Accepted for meta.budget parity; iterations is the effective cap here.

budget.description: meta.budget semantics (same shape as an AppSpec's meta.budget).

onFail.description: replan (default): apply the retained-lesson repair and iterate. stop: return after the first failing iteration.
